models.notes: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, registered 2026-07-29. This row carries no eval artifact ON PURPOSE: no measurement supports a predictive reading of the panel, and the one that exists refutes it. Three caveats must stay visible wherever it renders. (1) The strata are the output of a search over 3,957 overlapping cuts with no multiplicity correction, so extreme-looking groups are expected under the null. (2) The source artifact tools/_comb_out/archetype_descriptive_hit.json carries a health_warning claiming every stratum has a statistically zero out-of-fold residual against the shipped eFV model. That claim is FALSE as written: 477 of the 3,957 rows carry |t| >= 2 and 124 carry |t| >= 3. Do not repeat it in copy. (3) The script that produced that artifact, tools/_comb_sweep_desc.py, is ABSENT from the tree and nothing else in the repo writes that file, so mean WAR, median WAR, bust rate and the residual t cannot be regenerated or independently audited; they are a frozen quote of a 2026-07-25 measurement. Stratum MEMBERSHIP is reproducible and archetype_comps_export.py re-checks it on every run against the pre-registered outcome-blind enumeration (all 3,957 ids and resolved-row counts match, prereg sha16 fa70f4244573730b). Hitters only, decision years 2016-2024, 904 rows with 527 at a complete six-year window, reporting floor 25 complete-window players, base mean 1.90 WAR and 76.7 percent bust rate. Reader-facing methodology: glossary entry archetype_comps. SHIPPED FORM (archetype_comps_export.py): the false health_warning is dropped rather than propagated, and each stratum instead carries a reliability tier derived from its own t: priced 3,193 (|t| under 1.645, comps and grade agree), watch 687 (nominally off-model but not surviving Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 across all 3,957 tests, so unverified rather than a finding), off_model 77 (survives BH at |t| >= 3.30, comps and grade disagree, neither authoritative). Expected counts under a true global null are about 180 at |t| >= 2 and 11 at |t| >= 3, so the excess is real and is NOT purely a multiplicity artifact. Read the off_model tier with its shape attached: 76 of 77 carry a NEGATIVE residual and 43 busted at 100 percent, because WAR floors near zero for a player who never debuts, so any positive expectation on a young low-grade group is guaranteed a one-sided residual. That is the outcome scale bottoming out, not a correctable eFV defect, and the nested-CV NO SHIP verdict stands over all of it. 130 strata carry a zero-width WAR interval (every closed member realized the same value); degenerate, not precise.

ACCURACY IS A NULL AT 23x UNDERPOWER (d_spearman -0.00258 against a 0.0597 placebo half-width), so no claim either way is supported and the lane explicitly does not claim a gain. The org guard holds on 52 of 52 labels with zero rank-implied exposure. grade_normalization fits a separate offset per (source, role, cycle-year) and absorbs the 11.4 FV Adjusted-Grade era break. PROVISIONAL because two of four verifiers refuted parts of the headline and the lane's single load-bearing BLOCKER (the 2023 position gap) was already fixed before verification ran. Two findings outlive the lane: cross-year pooling is NOT BA-specific (138 of 176 live build_remapper cells pool, and (mlb_pipeline_international, hitter) 2021-2023 both pools AND fires on real rows), and the served eFV matrices no longer reproduce from the current corpus (74.8 percent of rows, 53.6 percent on busts). THE VINTAGE ARM FAILS AT ALL THREE QUANTILES: Brier delta -0.000505 (t -1.418, n_eval 213), -0.000115 (t -0.862, n_eval 160), -0.000004 (t -0.292, n_eval 104), log loss delta negative at all three as well, so Platt is not merely short of the bar, it is slightly WORSE than identity out of sample at every split. THE LEDGER ARM CANNOT COUNT: 49 of the 100 settled canonical moneyline games its pre-registered floor requires, stated in the doc before any number was computed, so the ship rule was unsatisfiable today whatever the vintage arm returned. THE PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION IS CONFIRMED, WHICH IS THE FINDING: diff_shrink is itself fitted on each fit half by minimizing log loss, so the response scale is already absorbed before Platt sees a probability; the fitted maps converge to identity as the fit window grows (a 1.137 -> 1.048 -> 1.005), and the residual two parameters only fit noise and pay for it held out. The moneyline's problem is DISCRIMINATION, not scale, and no monotone recalibration touches discrimination. SERVE_PROB_CALIBRATION stays False; the flag, the eval block and the tripwire in test_betting_platt.py move in one commit or not at all (the SERVE_RUN_DISPERSION pattern), and serving scope is moneyline only regardless - the runline and total stay behind the 11a dispersion gate. models.notes: Audit 2026-08-07b lane D1. MAGNITUDE CONFIRMED, LEAK NOT ESTABLISHED, and the two must not be conflated. The as-of repair moves consensus_fv_raw on 2,316 of 3,933 training rows (58.9 percent), by 0.5 FV or more on 29.5 percent, max 7.93 FV. Channel C1 (total_fv_instances counted with NO date filter at consensus.py:1248-1252 and passed as one scalar to every event date at :1298) moves 117 rows, mean abs 3.10 FV, max 10.42; the mechanism was hand-derived on tyler_skaggs (full-history instances 2 suppresses the FV-35 pull, as-of 1 fires it, 66.25 -> 58.333). Channel C3 (grade-norm thin-cell pooling) moves 2,286 rows, mean +0.940. CHANNEL C2 IS FALSE, AND THE REASON IS A BIGGER DEFECT THAN THE ONE IT DISPROVES: the drop-off detector matches a legacy '_org_' slug that occurs 0 times in 54,061 snapshots, so dropped_off_pairs returns the empty set on every run and the (fv+30)/2 shrink HAS NEVER FIRED IN PRODUCTION. Three verifiers confirmed it, one by calling consensus._dropped_off_pairs directly. That kills plan lane D-4 as written, which proposed FITTING that shrink on the grounds that it had 'better overlap and a real prior'; the overlap is exactly zero rows. THE LEAK CLAIM DID NOT SURVIVE: a zero-information control (adding only the per-fold MEAN delta as a per-decision-year constant) reproduces about 70 percent of the claimed d_rho, the C1 channel is null on every form the lane ran, and 1 of 6 pre-registered cells fires at p 0.016, which is Bonferroni p_adj 0.09 to 0.13. So C1 and C3 are CORRECTNESS repairs, argued from the fact that computing a historical point from the future is wrong, and never from a downstream rho. C3's repair is BLOCKED pending an owner decision: FanGraphs FV, the normalization reference, does not exist in the DB before 2017-02-15, so the as-of remapper returns None there and turns normalization OFF rather than computing an honest as-of offset, which would inject a 3 to 4 FV pre/post-2017 discontinuity into the model's dominant feature. Doc docs/efv-2026-08-07b/CONSENSUS_CONTAMINATION.md.

models.notes: Plan 2026-08-08 lane M4, pre-registered at docs/efv-2026-08-08/SHRINK_GATE.md before the lab existed. THE GATE IS THE INTERACTION, NOT POOLED delta-R^2: the registration refuses delta-R^2 because that effect is about 0.007 against an MDE of about 0.054, so pre-registering it would be pre-registering a null. RESULT: A2 IS A NULL AND THE INCUMBENT CONSTANT IS VINDICATED. Which x is used decides the question and running only one of them would invert the answer. On the PRE-shrinkage consensus a coverage dependence is visible, same sign both sides, hit beta +0.007519 (t 1.901, permuted-k p 0.107) and pit +0.006527 (t 2.215, p 0.048). On the POST-shrinkage consensus the board actually serves, it collapses to hit +0.000325 (p 0.944) and pit +0.001298 (p 0.712), i.e. the observed value sits dead centre of its own null band. The incumbent absorbs the mechanism almost exactly and is NOT detectably wrong. P1 fails even on the pre-shrinkage frame (paired bootstrap CI includes zero on both sides; per-year sign agreement 0.67 hit / 0.63 pit against a 3-of-4 bar), so the pre-registered stop clause applies: record the null and close A2 rather than hunting a gate that passes. LIMITS THAT BOUND THE VERDICT: coverage mass is almost entirely k=1 against k=2 (only 65 hit / 61 pit rows at k=3), which is where lambda_k differs LEAST, so this is not evidence that coverage is irrelevant at k=3; the two instruments disagree in emphasis on the pre-shrinkage pitcher cell (permutation p 0.048 against a bootstrap lower bound of -0.00007) and both are reported with no threshold moved after the fact; and resolved-only estimates attenuate (+0.0037 hit, +0.0013 pit), so part of the pre-shrinkage signal rides on censored rows. Do NOT ship a refit of SINGLE_SOURCE_K on this evidence. Sibling measurement in the same wave: per-source noise is identified label-free from pairwise overlap variances, and the within-year sigma ratio is 1.19 to 1.58, straddling its own 1.25 bar, with Baseball America the QUIETEST source in 2026 (the cross-year pooled 2.78x is an artifact of BA's 2026 basis change). Record docs/efv-2026-08-08/WAVE0_RECORD.md.

models.notes:
WS-5 (2026-06-11): vintage-disciplined A/B (weights for board-year Y from cohorts resolved before Y only) - weighted beat equal on BOTH pooled metrics (Spearman .2675 vs .2657, AUC .767 vs .759, n=3,127). Weights shrunk k=150 toward equal, clamped [0.6,1.5], vintage-frozen in data/source_weights.json (only move when a new base year resolves); sources without history pinned 1.0. Mechanics: consensus.compute_consensus_point source_weights kwarg; dispersion stats stay unweighted. TYPE-CONDITIONED WEIGHTS REJECTED (2026-06-11): separate hitter/pitcher accuracy weights (same estimator, same vintage rule) LOST to the shipped global weighting on both pooled metrics (Spearman .2705 vs .2717, AUC .7604 vs .7634, n=3,127) - the per-type common sets are too thin to beat the shrinkage. Loss committed: type_conditioned_ab block in the eval artifact (tools/consensus_type_ab.py). WEIGHTS REVERTED TO EQUAL 2026-07-25, recorded on this row 2026-07-29: data/source_weights.json now ships an EMPTY weight map, every source votes 1.0, and the champion string above describes what actually runs. The re-measured A/B (data/consensus_weight_eval.json, regenerated 2026-07-28, ship = False) reads equal 0.2728 Spearman / 0.7316 AUC against weighted 0.2737 / 0.7387 on n=2,858; the hardened ship rule requires the weighted arm to beat equal by more than the gate can resolve (d_rho >= 0.0068 = the measured MDE95, d_auc >= 0.0052) and it does not. Only 2 of 8 outlets have resolvable outcome history and their precisions are indistinguishable. The WS-5 weights (FG 0.939 / Pipeline 1.061) and the 2026-06-11 SURPRISE FINDING above are HISTORY, left on the row so the reversal is legible rather than silent. The report CARD was meant to be removed from this row at the same time: its headline pair (0.268 vs 0.267 Spearman, 0.744 vs 0.738 AUC) was that weighted-vs-equal comparison, which the 07-28 artifact supersedes and which is no longer a proof of anything shipped. It was not removed, and was replaced on 2026-09-11 (see CARD RE-DERIVED below). The blend-vs-best-single-source evidence this row's baseline names lives on row source_track_record (data/source_backtest.json), and that is what the validated verdict rests on. OPEN ITEM: this row's own eval_artifact measures the weighting choice rather than blend-vs-single-source, so the pointer and the baseline do not describe the same experiment; realigning them is an owner call, not a documentation edit. INPUT DEFECT FOUND 2026-07-30 (Phase 5.3 ingestion audit, docs/efv-2026-07-30/POSITION_ROLE_GATE.md, NOT FIXED - registered for an owner call): source `baseballamerica_statcast_by_age` writes a FABRICATED flat FV 40.0 (source_articles.py:230, our own editorial-standout floor, not a Baseball America grade) and votes in avg_fv at full weight 1.0 like a published grade. Its dedupe guard only checks whether the SAME BA article set ranked the player, not whether any other source has graded him, so 34 of its 41 rows land on players who already carry a real FV: mean avg_fv delta -1.201, median -1.042, worst -3.333 (alexander_frias and james_tibbs_iii, both 50.0 -> 46.67), 28 moved down and only 3 up. Compare `performance_ingest`, the other flat-constant source (FV 35.0 x 2,798 rows), which is honest by construction: 2,768 of its 2,798 players carry NO other grade, so it functions as the ungraded floor it was designed to be and collides with a real grade only 30 times. The fix is to widen the statcast_by_age guard from 'no ranked snapshot in this article set' to 'no explicit FV from any source', which changes served consensus values for 34 players and therefore needs its own gate. || FABRICATED-VOTE FIX 2026-07-30 (owner decision, LANE-SHIP). source_articles assigned a CONSTANT fv=40.0 to every row of the baseballamerica_statcast_by_age source - a number we invented, not a grade Baseball America published - and it voted in avg_fv at full weight 1.0. Its guard skipped a player only when THIS ARTICLE SET had already ranked him, not when any source had graded him, so 34 of the 41 live rows landed on players who already carried a real grade (83% collision, against performance_ingest's 30-in-2,798). The FV is REMOVED; the source is now identity plus statcast only, like BA's own Top 100 (100 rows, rank, zero FV). Measured through the real build_timeseries path over all 51,180 snapshots: 34 latest consensus points move, ZERO collateral movement outside the source; avg_fv mean +0.497 (median +0.210, range -2.500 to +2.710, 27 up / 7 down); served consensus_fv mean +0.324, 13 up / 6 down / 15 flat, best alexander_frias and james_tibbs_iii 46 -> 49. The DOWN movers are the same defect seen from the other side and are NOT a regression: on 7 players the invented 40 sat ABOVE their real grades (hyun_seung_lee, juan_villavicencio and richard_matic are all really FV 35 and were served 38), and jason_schiavone / luke_hill move up on avg_fv but down on served consensus because losing the fake vote drops them from 2 explicit-FV instances to 1 and correctly re-arms the single-instance shrinkage pull toward FV 35. THIRD CONSEQUENCE: 7 players (braylon_whitaker, easton_shelton, jacob_friend, jake_cunningham, jose_meza, mason_guerra, michael_martinez) have exactly ONE snapshot in the entire database - this one - and were on the board only because we graded them ourselves; with no FV and no rank they have no consensus point and LEAVE the board (ranks 373-1383, none in the top 300). Nothing is served differently until the next ingest re-parses the drop file and the UPSERT writes fv=NULL. performance_ingest was audited in the same pass and CLEARED: flat FV 35 on 2,798 rows but only 30 collisions, i.e. it functions as the ungraded floor it was designed to be.

IDENTITY: a systemic bind-time hole, FOUND 2026-08-04 and NOT yet closed. stats._apply_collision_guard has three checks and BOTH of the ones that matter require a DURABLE binding to already exist: check 2 fires when the KEY is already bound to a different id, check 3 when the ID is already bound to a different key. A key that has never been bound and an id that has never been bound sail past both. On 2026-08-04 a bulk pass wrote 712 bindings and three long-inactive records took the id of a currently-active same-slug stranger; every keyed write that followed (birth_date, roster_status, acquisitions, transactions, the fielding census) landed on the wrong human and needed a hand repair (tools/repair_merged_identities_2026_08_04.py).
AN AGE-COHERENCE GUARD WAS BUILT AND REJECTED, and the measurement is the useful part. The idea: refuse a binding when the id's birth date makes the subject impossibly young at the key's earliest snapshot, which is exactly the evidence that convicted all three (one was 9.6). Built DB-only, it FAILED BOTH WAYS. It caught NONE of the three target merges, because after repair the id's birth date resolves through the repaired binding rather than the newcomer's own record. And a sweep over the 7,606 current durable bindings found it would REFUSE 71 of them, about 1 percent, including julio_rodriguez, eury_perez and max_muncy - legitimate players whose key carries an earlier snapshot history than the human now holding it. A guard with a 1 percent false-refusal rate that catches none of its targets is worse than no guard, so it was reverted rather than shipped.
WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK: the check needs the RESOLVER'S OWN birthDate for the id being bound (PlayerIndex already carries it, stats.py:337/517) rather than a player_photos join that can pick up the wrong row, and it needs to compare against the snapshot history of the human rather than of the slug. That is a hot-path change to identity resolution and owes its own gate; the false-positive sweep above is the baseline it must beat.

models.notes: ENABLED 2026-07-25 by OWNER DIRECTIVE ('by the Clemens framework, hitter/pitcher FVs translate to different outcomes'), on a SPLIT gate. On the identity-WAR functional the effect is a NULL: gap@55 -1.87, bootstrap CI90 [-5.15, 1.31] (includes 0), inside the control band [-2.72, 2.69], permutation p 0.259, only 3/5 blocks negative. It RESOLVES on both variance-stabilized functionals: sqrt(WAR) gap@55 -2.57, CI90 [-5.30, -0.16], outside control, perm p 0.0495, 4/5 blocks; P(WAR>=3) gap@55 -2.76, CI90 [-5.41, -0.33], outside control, perm p 0.035, 4/5 blocks. JUSTIFICATION IS CROSS-SIDE COMPARABILITY, NOT A RANK LIFT -- a pooled-rank null is the EXPECTED result and must not be cited as evidence against it. SERVED EFFECT: max move 1.8 FV, 0 display inversions, top-25 pitcher share 0.04 -> 0.12 (1 -> 3 pitchers), top-100 0.09 -> 0.16; Seth Hernandez rank 29 -> 17, Ryan Sloan 50 -> 25, and the top 3 (Made / de Vries / Arias) are unchanged in order. === record as of 2026-08-04 (superseded on the basis question by the block above) ===
Built 2026-08-04 for the owner ask to move WAR off bWAR. fWAR was NOT an option: FanGraphs is Cloudflare-403 from this box (docs/efv-2026-07-30/DEFENSIVE_SOURCE_PROBE.md) and pybaseball's FG endpoint 403s, so eWAR is built from components already on disk.

VERDICT: DO NOT flip the site basis. eWAR LOSES the headline gate (team wins r 0.8595 vs bWAR 0.8803, zero-param MAE 4.306 vs 3.787) and WINS the persistence gate (FIP pitching self-r 0.3617 vs 0.1768 on the same 1,677 pairs, a 2.0x gain, and it forecasts NEXT year's actual runs above average better than THIS year's actual runs does, 0.2573 vs 0.1768).

Losing gate 1 was EXPECTED and is not evidence against the pitching swap. Gate 1 rewards describing the season that happened; B-Ref prices pitchers on the runs they actually allowed, which is most of what decided the games, so a runs-allowed WAR is close to mechanically fitted to team wins. FIP deliberately discards sequencing and balls in play, so it must fit worse in sample. ANY FIP-based WAR, fWAR included, loses this test.

THE ATTRIBUTION ARMS ARE THE REAL RESULT, because they run one swap at a time. The PITCHING swap costs same-season r (0.8595) and moves next-season signal to 0.2524 against the bWAR baseline 0.2481. READ THAT SECOND NUMBER WITH THE CORRECTION BELOW: it is a NULL, not a win. The pitching swap's forward case is at the PITCHER level (gate 2), not the team level. The FIELDING swap loses BOTH (0.8777 same-season, 0.2255 next-season) and therefore did not earn its place. Mechanical cause, and it generalises: Statcast OAA is a RANGE metric. It carries no outfield or infield ARM value, no catcher framing or blocking, no first-base scoops, no double-play pivot; B-Ref rfield does. Swapping OAA in for rfield is not a better metric for the SAME quantity, it is a better metric for a NARROWER one, and the value it drops is real. Catchers have zero OAA coverage by construction. data/savant_arm.json exists but is arm STRENGTH in mph from 2020, not runs, so it cannot close the gap without a model that does not exist.

FACE VALIDITY on the pitching half: it reproduces the known bWAR/fWAR divergences BY NAME and in the right direction, Aaron Nola 2018 9.69 -> 6.14 and Mike Minor 2019 7.99 -> 4.67, both toward their published fWAR. League sums land on the season target every year (about 999) so the accounting identity holds.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE VERDICT: an arm-value and catcher-framing run model so the fielding swap covers the same quantity rfield does; a BLEND of OAA and rfield rather than a replacement is CLOSED, do not re-run: it was built, swept over w = 0 to 1 and is monotone decreasing on BOTH the pooled and the full-schedule basis (see the v2 section); or re-running gate 1 against team runs scored and runs allowed separately instead of wins, which would separate component accuracy from the Pythagorean noise both series inherit.

NEXT STEP IF PURSUED: the pitching component is the part that is safe today, and the natural consumer is a FORWARD-looking one (eFV labels, projections) rather than a descriptive display, because forward use is exactly where a 2.1x persistence gain pays and where losing the descriptive gate does not matter. That is an owner call and it is a coordinated re-anchor, not a ride-along: it would require refitting the FV outcome curve, FV_EXPECTED_WAR, the survivor curve, the prospx FV_WAR_ANCHORS mirror, the draft slot curve and the empirical anchors, plus a label= term in BOARD_BASIS_FINGERPRINT.

=== v2, 2026-08-04: THE STATCAST FIELDING SWAP IS REMOVED ===
v1 replaced rfield with the Statcast read wherever Statcast covered the innings. v2 does not use Statcast fielding at all. A blend axis was built specifically to rescue it - w = weight on the Statcast read over covered innings, rfield taking the rest - and the grid over 2016-2025 (300 team-seasons, pitching swap on throughout, so w=0 is the pitching-only arm) settled it:
    w      wins r   wins mae0   next-yr r   prevention |r|
    0.00   0.8595     4.306      0.2524         0.3780
    0.25   0.8636     4.260      0.2491         0.3759
    0.50   0.8667     4.251      0.2452         0.3718
    0.75   0.8684     4.277      0.2408         0.3652
    1.00   0.8686     4.347      0.2359         0.3559
    bWAR   0.8803     3.787      0.2481         0.4290
BOTH FORWARD-LOOKING LEGS ARE MONOTONE DECREASING IN w, across five points and two independent gates. There is no weight at which the Statcast read pays for itself, so this is not a threshold to tune around. At w=0 eWAR loses same-season fit (0.8595 vs 0.8803) and is a NULL on the forward leg, NOT a win - see the correction section below, which supersedes any earlier claim that 0.2524 vs 0.2481 was a win.

NEW GATE 1b (team runs), added because team WINS are runs put through the Pythagorean relation and that noise is large enough to bury a component whose whole effect is a few runs a season - which fielding is. Components are scored against what they CAUSE: offence vs runs scored, fielding+pitching vs runs allowed, total vs run differential. It needed no new fetch; the cached StatsAPI standings already carried runsScored/runsAllowed and standings() was discarding them. The OFFENCE ARM IS AN EXACT NULL CONTROL at every w (r 0.3132 for both series), which is what licenses trusting the prevention comparison: no component leaked.

Endpoints verified on real rows before any result was read: w=1.0 reproduces the v1 default to 0.0 across all team-seasons, w=0.0 reproduces bWAR's rfield to 0.0 across 6,640 batter-seasons.

CATCHER FRAMING: probed and REFUSED. Savant's catcher-framing leaderboard responds and rv_tot is genuinely framing runs (validated internally - the per-zone integers sum to it), but the season parameter is INERT: year/season/startYear all return one identical undated payload (md5 b389177d5e). Ingesting it would assign a single snapshot to ten seasons. Recorded in the artifact so the next attempt starts from 'where does a season-resolved source live'.

A home-run regression variant on the FIP leg is implemented and DEFAULT OFF (fip_hr_shrink_k). It is deliberately not called xFIP: the corpus has no batted-ball profile, so there is no fly-ball denominator, and it regresses the HR rate itself instead. GATED 2026-08-04, NO SHIP - see the R2e.2 section below.

Verdict UNCHANGED at provisional and eWAR still ships to NO consumer. It loses the descriptive gate and wins the forward one; the natural first use remains a forward-looking consumer (eFV labels), which is R3 and is gated.

R2b, THE ERA TEST (2026-08-04, read off the per-season attribution the v2 rebuild emits). The range-only account of why the fielding swap loses makes a testable prediction: once Savant folded outfield ARM into its fielding run value around 2022, the metric covers more of what rfield covers, so the loss should SHRINK. It does. Mean fielding-swap delta against the per-season bWAR baseline: -0.0368 for 2016-2021 against -0.0194 for 2022-2025, a 1.90x narrowing; excluding the 60-game 2020 season, whose -0.0800 is the largest single value and a small-sample artifact, it is -0.0282 against -0.0194, still 1.45x. The direction is right and the mechanism is supported.
BUT IT IS NOT ELIMINATED. Every post-2022 season is still individually NEGATIVE (-0.0048, -0.0285, -0.0344, -0.0099), so even in the era where FRV is broadest the swap still costs same-season fit. That residual is what the range-only story does not cover, and the obvious candidates are the components the OF-arm addition never touched: catcher framing and blocking (zero OAA coverage by construction) and infield throwing.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WEIGHT: an era-aware w was the reason to run this, and the answer is DO NOT make w era-conditional. The optimum is at or near 0 in BOTH eras, so splitting the weight by era would add a parameter to buy nothing. w=0 stands whole-window. Sample is small (n=4 post) and the pre group carries a COVID outlier, so this is a supporting read, not a headline.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-04: THE FORWARD-LEG "WIN" WAS NOT REAL ===
Earlier revisions of this row, of ewar.py and of commit 744d525 all claimed that at w=0 eWAR BEATS bWAR on the forward leg, 0.2524 vs 0.2481. It does not. Refuted by two independent reviewers and reproduced from source before anything was edited. Three reasons, any one fatal:
  SCALE CONTAMINATION. 60 of the 270 forward pairs straddle the 60-game 2020 season, putting a 60-game season on one axis and a 162-game season on the other. Those 60 pairs correlate about -0.53 and drag the pooled r from roughly 0.59 down to 0.25. On full-schedule pairs only (both seasons >= 140 team games, n=210) it reads 0.5920 vs 0.5913, a delta of +0.0006.
  A ZERO-INFORMATION CONTROL BEATS IT. Shuffling the per-team eWAR-minus-bWAR delta across teams produces an absolute delta at least as large 82.3% of the time and beats bWAR outright in 27.3% of shuffles.
  IT IS CARRIED BY TWO PAIRS. Per year-pair eWAR wins 4 of 9 and LOSES the four most recent; the pooled edge comes from 2016->2017 (+0.176) and the COVID pair 2020->2021 (+0.119).
WHAT SURVIVES, and the distinction is the point: the w-grid that decided v2 is untouched. Re-run on full-schedule pairs the forward delta runs +0.0006 / -0.0019 / -0.0057 / -0.0108 / -0.0173 across w = 0 to 1, still MONOTONE DECREASING, so dropping Statcast fielding was right and is not an artifact of the 2020 problem. The w-grid compares eWAR variants against each other; the bWAR comparison is a different question and it is a null. eWAR's real case is at the PITCHER level (gate 2), where the persistence gain survives its controls, and it does not survive aggregation to the team. gate_team_wins now emits next_season_wins_full_schedule_only so this is visible in the artifact rather than only in prose.

=== TWO CONTROLS THAT COULD NOT FAIL, both fixed 2026-08-04 ===
1. EVAL WINDOW. evaluate() computed `last` to exclude the in-progress season and then passed it to TWO of six blocks. Persistence, coverage, accounting and face-validity ran UNWINDOWED, so the artifact declared eval_window [2016,2025] while four of its blocks measured 2016-2026: 148 of 1825 gate-2 pairs (8.1%) had the three-week-old 2026 as their y+1 target, and accounting reported a 2026 row with 3364 team-games inside a "max_abs_deviation 0.0" pass. Fixed by windowing the model ONCE (_window_model) and handing identical rows to every block. NO VERDICT MOVED, which is why it had gone unnoticed: gate 2 goes 0.3664/0.1769 -> 0.3617/0.1768 self and 0.2548 -> 0.2573 forecast, on 1,677 pairs rather than 1,825. What was wrong was the artifact describing a population it had not measured.
2. THE UNSHRUNK-FIELDING SENSITIVITY WAS BIT-IDENTICAL to the gate it claims to vary. The OAA reliability shrinkage multiplies the Statcast fielding term, and at the shipped w=0.0 that term is multiplied by zero, so an unshrunk build at the default reproduced gate 1 to the last decimal. Now pinned at fielding_blend_w=1.0, and evaluate() asserts the block is live and stamps `degenerate` rather than trusting the caller. It PASSED its own pre-registered rule in sample. Forecast leg (min_ip 50): k None 0.2548, 100 0.2665, 200 0.2725, 400 0.2782, 800 0.2782. Two discriminating controls rule out generic reliability weighting: the same exposure shrink on ALL THREE FIP rates gives 0.2222 at k=800 (worse than doing nothing) and on the K rate alone gives 0.1825, against 0.2782 for HR-only. The effect is home-run specific, exactly as hypothesised. DECLINED on two grounds the in-sample curve cannot see: it does not transport (+0.0017 on a temporal holdout, and the argmax moves k=1600 -> k=400 between eras, so it is fitting the era), and it collides with the w=0 decision (it drives the team forward leg monotonically below bWAR, 0.2421 at k=400). === R2e.3 RELIEVER LEVERAGE: RECORD AND STOP ===
Leverage is priced UPSTREAM and survives the FIP swap intact. B-Ref's reliever chaining lives in war_daily's WAA_adj, the identity WAR = WAA + WAA_adj + WAR_rep holds to a residual sd of 0.0029, and build() ingests WAR whole and never decomposes it. The alternative is dead on its own gate too: our gmLI (mlb_leverage) and B-Ref's are the same number, r = 0.9947 on 993 reliever-seasons, with a clean shuffle control at +0.0015. Do NOT re-propose crediting relievers with our own gmLI; it is a measured null.

=== R3a eFV LABEL SWAP: NO SHIP. UNSUPPORTED, NOT CLOSED ===
The owner's original hypothesis was that a better WAR label makes eFV more accurate. Decision quantity is the model-versus-consensus MARGIN with BOTH scored on the SAME labels, because swapping the label changes what "right" means and absolute rho is uninterpretable. DELTA = -0.0011 (hit) and -0.0115 (pit), both NEGATIVE, against MDE floors of 0.017 and 0.016. Coverage was not the obstacle: 98.6% of hit and 99.1% of pit test-fold rows carry an eWAR label, because the scored folds are debut years 2020-2023 and eWAR starts in 2016.
THE NULL IS NOT TIGHT ENOUGH TO CLOSE THE QUESTION. The lane's bootstrap held both fitted models FIXED, but the eWAR arm refits ridge and OLS on the new label, so model-estimation variance belongs in the sampling distribution. Adding it moves pit sd 0.0164 -> 0.0210 and the CI90 upper bound to +0.0206, ABOVE the 0.016 floor; the original single-seed CI90 upper of +0.0147 also sits within Monte Carlo error of the floor, and 10 of 40 reseeds put it at or above. So: no evidence of benefit, do NOT flip (R3c is NOT triggered), and do not write down that the hypothesis is closed. "Unsupported" is the honest and weaker claim.

R3a HIGHER-POWERED RE-TEST (owner-authorised, 2026-08-04): the question is STILL NOT CLOSED, and the original headline got WEAKER. Design pre-registered before running: add the 2019 fold (test 71, train 80) to take the scored pitcher population from 434 to 505 rows, and raise the full-refit paired bootstrap from B=400 to B=2000. The 2024 fold was deliberately EXCLUDED despite being larger, because a 2024 debut has only 2 of 6 label seasons resolved against 6 for 2019, so it would buy rows by degrading what the label means.
RESULTS. The base 4-fold arm reproduces exactly at DELTA -0.0115. On 5 folds DELTA is -0.0001, so the "eWAR moved the wrong way on pitchers" reading is FOLD-DEPENDENT and must not be quoted as stable. sd went 0.0210 -> 0.02393, WIDER, not narrower. The pre-registered prediction was a roughly 7% shrink from +16% n and it was WRONG: it treated all rows as equally informative, when the 2019 fold trains on 80 rows against 151+ for the folds it joins and therefore carries more noise than information (the margin over consensus falls from +0.0286 to +0.0104 on the bWAR label too). CI90 [-0.0469, +0.0311], upper bound still well above the 0.016 floor.
VERDICT UNCHANGED: unsupported, not closed, do not flip. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: not a re-slice of this cohort, which cannot be partitioned into enough power, but debut years maturing to six fully resolved label seasons. Revisit when 2021+ debuts resolve.

fa_backtest Gate 1 with the realized label swapped to eWAR: margin over the Marcel carry-forward baseline is -0.0387 WAR on pitchers against a pre-registered floor of +0.020, CI95 [-0.0472, -0.0309], negative in all six scored targets. Feeding the raw partial season made a durable regular briefly hurt this year (Lindor: 105 PA / 0.5 WAR vs his ~700 PA / ~6 WAR norm) read as a bad FULL season -> projected as a part-timer with an out-year cliff. Fix: reliability-blend the in-progress season's PT (fa_projection.project_player) AND the ML lag features war/exposure (proj_ml.build_features) toward the player's established (prior completed) level, weighted by the unobserved fraction (1-frac); healthy regulars whose current pace matches their track record are ~unchanged (population median y1 delta 0.000), only limited/injured veterans lift (mean +0.07). LIVE-ONLY: the gates project from completed seasons (in_progress=None), so Gate-1 (war 0.627, coverage 0.800) and Gate-2 are BYTE-UNCHANGED - re-confirmed PASS. Lindor 6.7 -> 12.2 5y WAR, cliff removed. Trade-off (disclosed): a player limited by losing the job, not injury, is also lifted - the lesser error for a star-heavy surface. P-IPAGE FIX (2026-07-24, projections lane): pitcher ip_proj was stamped BEFORE the pt aging delta, so the fitted pt curve (fit on BF) aged the exposure while war_from_projection - which reads ip_proj alone - never saw it, and the FIP algebra divided an AGED numerator by an UN-AGED denominator (older pitchers got BETTER FIPs). 72.8% of projected pitchers carried a >5% internal pt/ip inconsistency and shipped year-1 pitcher WAR was +83.1 too high in aggregate. ip_proj now follows pt_proj/4.3. GATE (7 forward-chained bases 2014-2021 ex-2020, 135 paired bootstrap draws, curves+WAR map refit per draw): pitcher h1 MAE 0.5566 -> 0.5339, delta -0.0231 CI95 [-0.0279,-0.0155], P(improve) 1.000, noise floor 1.96sd = 0.0073, permuted-age placebo +0.0069 (wrong sign). TOUCHED-ONCE HOLDOUT 2022-2024: pitcher h1 -0.0305 CI95 [-0.0375,-0.0233] P 1.000, pitcher all-horizon -0.0124 CI95 [-0.0181,-0.0053], 3/3 splits negative. Level bias improves at EVERY horizon (pit h1 +0.0477 -> -0.0007, h5 -0.0855 -> -0.0702). DISCLOSED NULL: h3-h5 MAE moves +0.005 to +0.009 with CIs straddling zero. P-CTTL FIX (2026-07-24): build_corpus accepted its cache whenever cached['last'] >= date.today().year, which is permanently true inside a season - the pickle never expired. Measured: a corpus frozen 2026-06-23 (88,517 league PA, season_fraction 0.484) served a payload stamped 2026-07-24 against a StatsAPI cache refetched that morning. Now invalidates when a source file for the in-progress season is newer than the pickle, or after CORPUS_TTL_DAYS=3, fail-soft to the stale cache on any source failure and refusing to overwrite a good cache with a degenerate (empty-bWAR) rebuild. After: 116,850 PA, season_fraction 0.6388. P-LGPIT MEASURED NON-SHIP (2026-07-24): the league HITTER denominators include pitchers batting pre-2022 (K% +0.0058, 76% of the observed 2021->2022 step). Removing it LOST resolvably - hitter h1 MAE +0.0191 CI95 [+0.0174,+0.0207] against a 0.0018 floor, hitter h1 bias +0.0289 -> +0.0745; the narrower regression-target-only variant still cost +0.0145. The contamination is an unintended deflator offsetting a structural hitter over-projection; the league means and the hitter level must be re-fitted together. FA LANE PHASE E2/E3/E4a (2026-07-30), criteria pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/FA_LANE_GATES.md, lab tools/fa_projection_lab.py -> data/fa_projection_lab_eval.json. TWO ARMS SHIPPED, ONE MEASURED LOSS. (E2, F-REALWAR) The WAR map's only positional term is a catcher dummy while its target is bWAR, which includes defense and positional value; measured consequence on the forward-chained Gate-1 panel: for the 424 hitter-seasons that actually produced >=4 bWAR the map predicts a mean 2.34 against 5.56 actual, and the naive 5/4/3 carry-forward BEATS the model in that cell (2.37 vs 3.23). Added a realized-bWAR RESIDUAL channel: the map's own prediction for each of the player's up-to-three prior seasons is reconstructed from the map's own features and subtracted from realized bWAR, exposure-weighted with the Marcel weights, capped at +-2.5 WAR per 600 PA / 100 IP, and shrunk on effective exposure (K = 1200 PA / 400 IP, fixed a priori). The RESIDUAL form is deliberate: blending realized WAR directly - the literal reading of the owner ask - double counts the offensive rate already flowing through the wRAA term, and because the map is a pooled least-squares fit the residual is orthogonal to its features on average, so the channel can only carry what the map cannot represent. Pooled WAR MAE 0.61572 -> 0.60087, delta -0.01496 CI95 [-0.01814,-0.01178], MDE95 0.00270, 10/10 folds; hitters 0.75957 -> 0.72509; wRC+/FIP byte-identical; coverage 0.799 -> 0.799. DISCLOSED PROTOCOL NOTE: the pre-registered clause was written as |delta_candidate| >= 3*|delta_control|, a magnitude form that presumes a control which could accidentally help; it reads False here only because the control's delta has the OPPOSITE SIGN, and both readings are recorded in the artifact (control_literal_3x_form). DISCLOSED RESIDUAL MISS: the >=4-bWAR cell improves (mean predicted 2.34 -> 2.66, cell MAE 3.235 -> 2.922) but is STILL worse than the naive baseline there - the star tail remains this engine's weakest region. (E3, F-PTFIT mode 'hit') The hand-set PT Marcel (0.5*PA1 + 0.1*PA2 + 200) was refit by OLS on corpus seasons <= 2014 - strictly before the first scored fold, so one fixed vector is ex-ante for all ten - with an added established-workload channel b3*max(0, three-season peak - platform). models.notes:
GATE 3 (first fit backtest ever): v2 hand weights barely beat random (MRR .142 vs .133), LOST to behavior-alone (.152). Fitted logistic (behavior .67) hit MRR .165 but was nearly player-independent (LAD topped all 133 pitcher lists). Shipped mix: gate-equivalent-or-better (MRR .167) AND player-discriminative - full comparison in the artifact. Caveats: reduced ex-ante analog (roster need/window not reconstructable); incumbency excluded by product design (ceiling MRR .270, measured). FITS v4 (2026-07-30), owner program Phase F, criteria pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/FA_LANE_GATES.md section F. THE FAILURE, measured on the served 2027 board (228 members, full 30-club vectors): LAD was the #1 fit for 154 of 228 (68%), only 6 clubs were ever #1, only 12 of 30 ever appeared in a top-3, the median #1-vs-#2 gap was 0.0180 (i.e. the ordering was noise), and SFG was #1 for 85% of pitchers projecting >=1.0 WAR. FIVE REPAIRS SHIPPED. F1 the need roster is now the PROJECTED roster read from data/mlb_projections.json (vets under club control for the class year INCLUDING the 361 thru=None arb/pre-arb rows, plus prospects with eta <= class_year) with the Spotrac scrape as a flagged fallback via _rosters()/roster_source, which also removes a live-scrape dependency from a serve path: 965 rows / 857.5 projected WAR against the Spotrac-only 858 / 741.2. DEFECT FOUND AND WORKED AROUND, worth recording: mlb_projections.json carries `team` ONLY on rows that joined a Spotrac contract, so all 361 arb/pre-arb rows have team=None and the artifact ALONE cannot say which club controls Jazz Chisholm Jr.; the org (and a real position for the 149 rows whose pos is the generic 'H') comes from the 40-man rosters StatsAPI already caches for /projections/, on the same _fetch keys and TTL, so no new network dependency. 253 vet rows still resolve to no org and are dropped. F2 the slot rule falls back to the WEAKEST player actually at the position instead of asserting 0.0 whenever len(inc) <= slot (v3 handed MAXIMUM need to any club with <= 4 contracted starters, which with an arb-blind roster was most of the league); added roster_completeness / n_at_position / n_controlled to the need decomposition; and the SILENT DROP is fixed - the org universe is the 30 clubs, not 'clubs with a qualifying row', because fit_scores iterates needs.items() and an absent club was absent from every player's vector (the MIA-has-no-baseWins defect). F2b, ADDED MID-PROGRAM AND PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE RUNNING after F1-F4 measured a REGRESSION (68% -> 79%): need is the ONLY player-specific component, so for any player whose need is flat across the 30 clubs the ranking IS a fixed club ranking and one club takes every such player - and v3's min(1, gap/4.0) capped a 0.8-WAR reliever's cross-club need spread at 0.2 (x weight 0.40 = 0.08) against behavior's ~0.65 (x 0.45 = 0.29), so behavior decided the ranking for most of the class by construction. NEED_MODE 'share' asks what FRACTION of the player's own projected value is additive at that club, min(1, gap / max(war_y1, 1.0)), giving every player a full 0-1 spread instead of only stars. F3 the window term blends marginal leverage with the LEVEL of postseason probability at the club's projected class-year win total (FIT_WINDOW_LEVEL_W = 0.6, the smallest level weight that makes the ordering constraint hold for EVERY input pair rather than on average). v3's 4p(1-p) is symmetric bubble-proximity, so a 0%-playoff SFG scored 0.828 against a locked-in LAD's 0.175; now SFG 0.323 against LAD 0.650. The plan named team_outlook[].current.playoffPct; it is NOT consumed because it is the IN-PROGRESS season's probability rather than the contract season's AND the artifact is missing the entire `current` block for ARI (reads null 2026-07-29, a defect in that artifact) - deriving the level from the club's own projected class-year wins through the curve the module already documents keeps one definition for all 30 clubs and imputes nothing. The served playoffPct rides the component output as a cross-check. F4 behavior's will-spend term is now the SHARE of the club's own historical guarantees at least this large (_spend_reach) instead of min(1, max_guarantee/price)**0.5, whose clip pinned it at 1.0 for nearly every player and turned the highest-weighted component into a per-club constant taking at most three distinct values across 223 members. fa_fit_backtest.build_rows was updated to MIRROR it, so Gate 3 scores what ships (the standing lesson of test_gate_scores_the_weights_that_actually_ship): Gate-3 MRR 0.1669 vs 0.1673 for the clipped form, i.e. neutral within the artifact's own 0.0126 MDE95. CONCENTRATION TRIPWIRE REGISTERED (fa_fit_backtest.concentration_gate, thresholds in CONCENTRATION_GATE, block `concentration` in this artifact) - MRR and top-k are blind to a fit vector that ranks the same club first for everyone. BEFORE -> AFTER: max #1 share 0.68 -> 0.5219 (gate <= 0.25, FAILS), distinct clubs #1 6 -> 10 (gate >= 12, FAILS), distinct clubs in any top-3 12 -> 20 (gate >= 20, PASSES), median #1-vs-#2 gap 0.0180 -> 0.0530 (gate >= 0.015, PASSES). So 2 of 4 registered metrics pass and the gate as a whole DOES NOT PASS; this is reported as a partial result, not a win. THE RE-WEIGHT IS A NO-SHIP AND THE WEIGHTS ARE UNCHANGED at need .40 / window .05 / afford .05 / park .05 / behavior .45. Seven candidate vectors were scored on BOTH gates on identical folds: every vector that improves concentration materially loses Gate-3 MRR by more than the pre-registered 0.010 band (need .50/beh .25 -> 0.1538, need .60/beh .15 -> 0.1449, which also falls below behavior_only at 0.1515), and every vector inside the Gate-3-equivalent neighbourhood (including the newly fitted logistic, which now lands need-DOMINATED at .596 with MRR 0.1660) leaves max #1 share at 49-52%. LAD's dominance survives every mix because it genuinely leads on need, on spending history and on the 2027 window at once. The two gates disagree and the pre-registration says Gate 3 binds for weight changes, so nothing was tuned; the trade-off is handed to the owner with numbers. THE FIFTH REGISTERED METRIC IS MIS-SPECIFIED AND IS REPORTED, NOT GATED: 'max share of #1 fits within one side' cannot be satisfied by any correct additive composite, because within a position group the need ordering is a property of the CLUBS and not of the player. SFG is still #1 for 85% of pitchers projecting >=1.0 WAR, but it now wins on a real continuous margin (its 5th-starter slot projects 0.00 WAR against a next-thinnest 0.03 and a league median near 0.85) rather than on the v3 pathology, and across ALL pitchers the top club is LAD at 54%. RESIDUAL DATA LIMIT, disclosed: SFG carries only 5 SP against a league range of 5-11 because pitcher positions come from Spotrac labels (the 40-man codes every pitcher as 'P'), so some of that thinness is label noise rather than roster fact. ARTIFACT REPAIR IN THE SAME CHANGE: weight_mix_comparison and ship_decision, which two pinned tests assert, existed ONLY in the committed artifact and were produced by NO code - any persist=True re-run silently deleted them and broke the pins. Both are now computed by run_fit_gate from the same pooled groups as every other row.

=== 2026-08-04 CONCENTRATION ROOT CAUSE: it is BEHAVIOR, not need ===
Four rounds of hand re-weighting had failed to fix max_top1_share, on the working assumption that the need component was saturated. DECOMPOSED per component (each scored as if it were the whole fit) plus a player/club/interaction variance split, on the served 228-member class. THE ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG.
  need     top1 0.5263 (ARI, on 8.10 clubs tied on average), club effect 3.9%, and it supplies 75.6% of the composite's ENTIRE interaction. It is the HEALTHIEST component.
  behavior top1 1.0000 (LAD, 228 of 228, zero ties), club effect 69.8% vs 1.4% interaction. At weight 0.45 it contributes 63.7% of the composite club main effect.
ONE LEVEL DEEPER, and this is the mechanism: behavior = 0.5*reach + 0.3*recent + 0.2*rich, and ONLY reach takes a player input. The F4 repair to reach WORKED (LAD tops raw reach at just 5 of 41 sampled price points). But `recent` divides by the league-max 3-winter outlay, which IS LAD, so LAD scores exactly 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION, and `rich` clips at n_100m/5, saturating for 5 clubs. Those two player-INDEPENDENT constants hand LAD a 0.500 floor against NYM 0.422 and a league median of 0.077 before the free agent is consulted, and LAD tops the full behavior blend at 41 of 41 price points. No re-weighting can reach a constant, which is exactly why four rounds of it failed.

CANDIDATES ALL NO-SHIP, same 1,173-signing forward chain: per-player z-scoring of the composite is a PROVEN NO-OP (a positive affine transform within each player; ranking bit-identical for all 228 - recorded so it is never proposed again); club-mass cap and relative-fit are per-club additive offsets that buy concentration with accuracy one-for-one, losing 0.020-0.026 MRR, roughly 2x the harness MDE95 and larger than the entire shipped-over-behavior_only edge. Neither can EVER clear the four-criterion gate: min_median_gap and max_top1_share are in mechanical tension along the whole offset family, because the number-1-versus-2 gap IS the club effect. Concentration and MRR measure opposite halves of one variance split.

A 10,626-point simplex sweep found 386 weight vectors that clear all four criteria, and the lane declined to recommend the best of them, correctly: it has ZERO slack (distinct_top1 exactly at the minimum), only 8 of the 386 reach shipped MRR, and it zeroes window and afford while DOUBLING park, the component fa_config itself records as the cause of the Giants-for-all-pitchers failure. Also proved: the need/behavior line with the other three pinned at 0.05 has ZERO passers, which is why hand-tuning that line could never have worked.

SHIPPED WEIGHTS UNCHANGED. The tripwire stays RED and honest. The real repair is to make `recent` and `rich` player-conditional so behavior stops carrying a constant, and that is a model change owing its own gate.

=== 2026-08-19 TEAMFIT CONDITIONAL: GATE PASS, THEN WIRED LIVE ===
The player-conditional behavior repair the 2026-08-04 note called for ran under a frozen gate (docs/fa-2026-08-19/TEAMFIT_CONDITIONAL_GATE.md; block teamfit_conditional_gate in data/fa_gate3_eval.json): recent/rich confined to the player's own price band [g/2.5, g*2.5], reach untouched, no weight moves. ALL FOUR CLAUSES PASS: chain MRR 0.1628 vs incumbent 0.1669 within MDE95 0.0139 (cluster bootstrap B=2000 seed 7; delta CI95 [-0.0184, +0.0091] straddles zero; top3 0.1338 vs floor 0.1311, margin 0.0027, slim and disclosed); served-class concentration GREEN at max top-1 share 0.2174 (WSN, not LAD) / 16 distinct top-1 / 25 distinct top-3 (n=230); LAD behavior top-1 share falls 1.0000 -> 0.3826, i.e. the constructed floor is gone; and the 10,626-vector zero-slack trade did not repeat, because the banded terms carry interaction instead of a per-club constant. Disclosed: top5 (a stated headline metric, not a frozen clause) degrades 0.2293 -> 0.2097; the incumbency ceiling (fitted_full MRR 0.2679) stays excluded by product design. WIRED LIVE in a second change: fa_fit.fit_scores computes the banded terms behind fa_config.fit.behavior_conditional, and the flag flipped true only AFTER the artifact recorded shipped=true (evidence ordering pinned by test_fa_teamfit_conditional.py). The artifact's top-level concentration block still carries the 2026-08-04 class (n=228, max share 0.5746) until the next full regen; the R6.3 'do not re-attempt a behavior-only repair' comments are superseded (their 0.3816 behavior-deleted falsification does not reproduce on the current class: 0.2913, MIA).

Pitchers (2026-09-11, owner decisions 13 and 14a): priced on FanGraphs' IFFB, Guts FIP park factor, Start-IP and the catcher framing earned on each pitcher's pitches (fwar_frame convention 9), all from the fg_leaderboards cache, pitcher RAR clears the gate in 6 of 15 completed seasons (2011, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2023, 2025; 0 before) and sits at 97.9 to 98.97 percent within 1.0 run in the other nine; the leave-one-out FIP- factor in place of the Guts factor clears 9. The remainder is traded pitchers, priced on season totals (per-stint counting stats are not on disk). FIP reproduces exactly. FanGraphs CFraming matches the feed's framing residual within 0.01 runs for every catcher but one (0.03). Nothing served reads this module; it is the faithful frame every eWAR v3 improvement arm must be measured against.

=== 2026-09-06 BASIS RE-STAMP (lane pal_restamp): LABELLING ONLY, NOTHING RE-FITTED OR RE-GATED ===
The served page and the gate are on TWO DIFFERENT WAR series, and now they say so. pal_export.load_bref_pitcher_war reads war_source.DEFAULT_PROVIDER, which the 2026-09-03 epoch moved to eWAR v2, so the live stamp in data/pal.json (generated_at 2026-09-05) reads rho +0.025 RP->SP (n=25) and +0.278 SP->RP (n=61), while this row's metric, data/pal_eval.json (generated_at 2026-07-15), the glossary and docs/e3-rp-sp-closure.md all cite -0.2062 and +0.2916 from the bWAR basis. NO GATE WAS RE-RUN: the pass/fail verdicts stand exactly as measured on bWAR, and RP->SP moving from sign-wrong (-0.2062) to null (+0.025) under the label swap is an UNGATED observation, not a new verdict.
WHAT SHIPPED. data/pal.json backtest now carries war_basis (the provider that produced the live rhos, its one-line description and the run date) and gate (the per-direction verdict carried out of data/pal_eval.json with the series IT was measured on, its n_gate, its best baseline and the gap lo95, plus same_basis_as_live=false). assets/pal.js DERIVES every validity word from those blocks: the scorecard, the section notes, the page banner and both shareable-board captions. It used to print 'validated vs baselines' and 'does not validate ranking' as literal strings, so the card could not change its verdict when the measurement changed; a payload with no gate block now reads 'gate verdict not in this payload' rather than asserting one, and the sign of a live rho is never promoted to a verdict. STILL OWED: re-running the pre-registered gate on the eWAR v2 label (plan lane PAL-1's first half) was NOT done and is not licensed by this stamp; docs/e3-rp-sp-closure.md still forbids re-gating RP->SP by expanding the event set. data/pal_eval.json, the glossary (rp_sp_fit / sp_rp_fit / pal_conversion) and the closure doc still quote the two rhos without naming the WAR series they were measured on.

=== 2026-09-25 MEAN-REVERSION CAVEAT (final pass M07-01): DISCLOSURE ONLY, NOTHING RE-GATED ===
The SP->RP pass rests on baselines that are all signed so a BETTER pre-season predicts a bigger gain (K-BB%, negated ERA, SEM+), while war_delta pays out on a BAD pre-season. Read the other way, the gate's own negated-ERA baseline (-0.62 in data/pal_eval.json) ranks the 61 gate events at +0.62 against FIT's +0.2916, and FIT scales with starter ERA through its conversion-need term (pal_conversion.sp_rp_fit). So the note above that the need-gated screen 'carries real signal vs naive quality reads' holds only against quality reads; it does not hold against a need read. pal_export now carries each direction's baseline rhos and the reversed read (reversed_baseline, reversed_baseline_rho, reversed_beats_fit) in backtest.gate, and the /pal/ masthead, banner, share captions, SP->RP note and History scorecard print the caveat beside the verdict word, which is unchanged. A re-gate with need-direction baselines is a new pre-registration that needs owner sign-off, sequenced after the fWAR season-close epoch; the RP->SP closed-event set stays closed per docs/e3-rp-sp-closure.md.

RESOLVER: 2,674 of 2,675 census players resolve; 1,957 join the served board and 476 of those (24.3%) disagree outright with the FG projection. The disagreement is SIGNED - FG projects a move DOWN the defensive spectrum 318 times against 184 up (1.73:1) - which is why position is NOT repointed and why positional scarcity is NOT repointed: paying 318 players a premium-position premium the industry says they will not hold is the single most expensive way to get this wrong. SHIPPED FLIPS, measured on the 2026-07-30 tree: D-Tool catcher weighting - 156 covered rows change bucket, 44 cross the catcher boundary (the only crossing that changes a weight) and only 9 of those have a composite_def to move; best-ranked is josue_briceno (served 1B, observed C, rank 65). composite_def is display-only (D-Tool pill + tool flag), not a board input. If turned on today, pos_prem would change 327 of 1,956 live rows and 10 rows inside the served top 100 (caleb_bonemer 22, kevin_alvarez 26, jojo_parker 30, edward_florentino 34, charles_davalan 35, josue_briceno 65, josh_adamczewski 67, francisco_renteria 70, elian_pena 81, emmanuel_rodriguez 87), and def_value would change 225 of 613 covered matrix rows' milb_vector. UNBLOCKING: rebuild positions_played.json without the pre-debut filter (for pos_prem) and build an AS-OF per-season census (for def_value), then run the eFV / ladder gates. Both are DATA builds, not modelling calls. UNVALIDATED because 'most games played' is a definition, not a prediction; the flipped consumers are display cohorts whose own metrics have not moved.

models.metric: forward-chained Spearman Y->Y+1 RA9 (bootstrap CI on the rho gap) + leverage-variant bake-off + split-half stabilization + AAV market check
models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-30 (/mlbstats/ Bullpen Leaderboards), FULL validation. Forward-chained OOS 2018-2025 (ex-2020): REM+ predicts next-year RA9 at rho 0.236 vs raw FIP 0.211, ERA 0.090, raw WPA 0.106; bootstrap CI on the rho gap beats ERA (lo95 +0.088), beats raw WPA (lo95 +0.068), and edges its raw-FIP parent (lo95 +0.001) - so the empirical-Bayes shrinkage + reliever-pool anchoring earn their place. TWO-NUMBER design EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: the leverage-weighted variant bake-off (REM+_lev = 100+(REM+-100)*(1+d*(gmLI-1))) is monotone-WORSE in d (optimal damping d=0: rho 0.236 at d=0 -> 0.227 at d=1.0), so folding gmLI in only hurts forward prediction (gmLI is manager-assigned, not repeatable skill; Moore 2011). YET the MARKET CHECK (271 matched RP FA signings, data/fa_archive.json) shows leverage-weighted REM+ correlates with AAV slightly BETTER (0.516) than pure (0.508): teams PAY for leverage. Conclusion (Rosen 2026): leverage is a price/deployment layer, not a talent layer -> kept OUT of the 100-scale REM+, surfaced in separate Impact columns (gmLI/WPA/WPA-LI/SD-MD). STABILIZATION: split-half REM+ rho rises with sample (0.18 @50-100 BF, 0.34 @100-150, 0.42 @150-250; relievers are genuinely volatile), qualifying at 100 BF sits at the knee. DATA self-computed from the StatsAPI winProbability feed (gmLI/WPA; FanGraphs 403-blocked), backfilled 2018-2025 via tools/backfill_win_prob.py (~17k games cached). v1 anchors on FIP not xFIP (xFIP needs a fly-ball walk). Bullpen+ = relief-IP-weighted REM+ rollup (leverage out) + a separate leverage-deploy column. Harness tools/rem_plus_backtest.py. X-S4 (Statcast xwOBA-allowed) TESTED + REJECTED 2026-07-06: over 6 Savant year-pairs (592 starter pairs), xwOBA-allowed forward-predicts next-year RA9 at rho 0.377 vs FIP 0.382 (a 0.5x/0.5x blend 0.384, gap vs FIP lo95 -0.053, CI spans 0), so contact-quality-allowed is redundant with what FIP already strips out; the FIP core stays. (Unlike hitters, where xwOBA strips the batter own BABIP luck and DID beat actual wOBA -> shipped xHEM+.) HARNESS-V2 RESTAMP COMPANION (2026-07-15, tools/rem_plus_lab.py): data/rem_plus_eval_restamp.json re-measures the shipped forward block on the lab pool (ex-openers, complete-outcome-season pairs only, unrounded rem_plus_raw) under BOTH conventions - v1 rho 0.2374 vs raw FIP 0.211 (gap lo95 +0.0023) and v2 (within-outcome-season z target, player-clustered season-stratified bootstrap) rho 0.2374 vs FIP 0.2172 (gap lo95 -0.0043; clustered CIs are wider by design and the shipped verdict STANDS per the pre-declared interpretation rules). The restamp closes the 0.2363-vs-0.2254 two-incumbent drift; data/rem_plus_eval.json remains the verdict authority and this row's eval artifact. MARKET CHECK SUPERSEDED (2026-09-24, census M06-01): the 271-signing check above joined players by normalized name, and its 0.516 belongs to the leverage-weighted lab variant, which no column serves. The /mlbstats/ scorecard printed that 0.516 under REM+'s name; it now copies REM+'s own figure from the 2026-09-18 re-gate (data/riv_market_regate_eval.json B1_primary v1.rho_baseline 0.5665 on 232 matched signings, descriptive). The leverage-weighted variant was not re-measured on that set, and the next market read waits for 2027-03-01.

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07 (Wave B1) as the realized-VALUE companion to REM+. CLAIM REFUTED and the row DEPRECATED 2026-09-18 by the pre-registered re-gate against REM+ (docs/HEM_RIV_REGATE_GATE.md, arm B1). This is a realized-value record, not a forecast, and that sentence travels with the row. WHAT THE RE-GATE FOUND, on 232 matched RP signings over seven winters (2019-2026), one target and one scale: RIV+_served correlates with AAV at 0.5733 and REM+ at 0.5665; the paired gap is mean 0.0052, lo95 -0.0953, hi95 0.1086 under v1 against an in-run MDE95 of 0.0862, and mean 0.0073, lo95 -0.0952, hi95 0.0997 under v2 (MDE95 0.082). The lower bound sits below -MDE95 under both conventions, which is the pre-registered refutation trigger. SAID PLAINLY SO THE ROW IS NOT MISREAD: RIV+ is NOT shown to be WORSE than REM+. The point estimate still favours it and hi95 stays well above zero. It is shown NOT TO BE BETTER, and 'better than REM+' was the only claim the row made. The published edge (0.576 against 0.508 over 271 name-matched signings) does not survive the correction: on one target, one scale, a walk-year TBF >= 100 floor and canonical MLBAM identity, REM+ reads 0.5665 rather than 0.508 and the edge collapses from +0.067 to +0.005 with a confidence interval of roughly plus or minus 0.10. The published number was a pair-set artifact, not a finding. WHY THE OLD EVAL COULD NOT ESTABLISH ITS CLAIM, as code facts: it compared two different targets on two different scales; one of its two PASS clauses (riv_less_stable_than_rem) can be passed by ADDING NOISE; it carried no interval anywhere on the market comparison; its floor was a hard-coded 0.02; identity was normalized-name only with no receipts; rows were un-clustered although relievers sign in several winters; and it scored riv_raw while the board serves the re-standardized composite, so pooled across winters the evaluated index and the served index were not the same statistic. Both the 0.02 slack and the noise-rewarding PASS clause are RETIRED in tools/rem_plus_lab.py as of 2026-09-18. DISCLOSURE LEG, zero verdict weight, asked correctly (one target at a time, 878 pairs): REM+(Y) predicts next-year RIV+ better than RIV+(Y) does, 0.2943 against 0.2020 (gap lo95 +0.0422 v1, +0.0371 v2), and REM+ predicts next-year REM+ at 0.3601 against RIV+'s 0.1847. Its interpretation was fixed in advance: this CONFIRMS that RIV+ carries a large non-repeatable deployment and sequencing component, which is consistent with the two-number design and is not itself a failure, but it FORBIDS any forward reading of the RIV+ column. On the shipped artifact data/riv_plus_eval.json the year-to-year rank correlation is 0.2023 against 0.3601 for REM+, and those figures are unchanged. COVERAGE, reported separately and never used to explain the gap: 573 RP signings with an AAV sit in data/fa_archive.json (git blob 7ee3ca5dcd86); 232 matched (226 through the canonical MLBAM path, 6 through the normalized-name fallback), 232 dropped for a walk year outside the scored seasons, 68 for unresolved identity and 41 for a walk-year TBF below 100. Three normalized-name collisions exist in the pool (javy_guerra twice, austin_adams once) and are published rather than assumed away. A RULE MIS-SPECIFICATION WAS FOUND IN RUN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY: the pre-registered 'not separable' band (lo95 <= 0 but lo95 > -MDE95) is unreachable for a gap centred near zero, because lo95 is roughly mean - 1.96*sd while -MDE95 is -1.645*sd, so the band needs mean > 0.315*sd. A dead-centre null therefore lands in the REFUTED row. The rule was applied as written because it is harsher than its own intent and softening a pre-registered outcome after seeing it is the move the gate exists to forbid; the next re-gate fixes the band rather than inheriting it. DISPLAY DEBT, recorded because another lane owns the page: the RIV+ column still ships on /mlbstats/ Bullpen Leaderboards and the data/glossary.json riv_plus entry claimed 'RIV+ tracks what teams pay relief free agents at least as closely as REM+ (rank correlation with AAV 0.58 against 0.51 over 271 signings)'. That sentence is refuted; on 2026-09-24 (census X07-01) it was replaced by the re-gate reading (0.573 against 0.567 on 232 signings, gap inside the noise floor), pinned in test_claims_freshness.py. The column itself still ships and is an open display question. The registry grades claims, not pixels, so the verdict moves now and the copy follows. Harness tools/riv_market_regate_lab.py; the index is computed live in rem_plus.score_riv_plus. Next market re-read 2027-03-01, after the 2026-27 free-agent class closes; reading a partially signed winter is a disqualifying look because the top of the market signs first.

THE HEADLINE FINDING IS A NEGATIVE ONE and lives in docs/efv-2026-07-30/CONVERSION_ARM_GATE_VERDICT.md: the mph is heavily conditioned on THROW CONTEXT, not arm talent. Same player, same season, throwing from two spots reads +3.69 mph from 3B vs 2B and +7.46 from the outfield vs the infield (98% of 102 pairs). models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-31 as Rng+ (legs), display only, gate at docs/efv-2026-07-30/SPRINT_RANGE_GATE.md. THE FINDING IS THE RESTRICTION. Against OAA per 1000 innings at the position played: CF r=+0.428 CI [+0.342,+0.507] n=378, LF +0.416 [+0.323,+0.501] n=331, but SS -0.020 [-0.122,+0.083] and 3B -0.004 [-0.108,+0.100]. Sprint speed predicts outfield range and measures a flat zero on the dirt, so the meter renders on LF and CF destinations ONLY; a speed read on a shortstop row would show a reader a measured nothing. RIGHT FIELD IS EXCLUDED despite clearing the headline bar (+0.269 [+0.167,+0.365]): its PURE-CORNER subgroup, right fielders with under 100 career CF innings, is r=+0.075 [-0.111,+0.256] and cannot clear zero, so the RF signal is carried by displaced centre fielders and the column would be telling corner-only right fielders something never measured on players like them. LF survives the identical test at +0.359 [+0.163,+0.528] n=89 and is not restriction-of-range (pure-corner sprint sd 0.79 vs 0.97 for all LF). THIS IS THE SURVIVING HALF OF OWNER ASK 1: the arm half was NO-SHIPPED because within the same player in the same season throwing from two spots the outfield reads +7.46 mph over infield on 102 pairs, so 3.69 of the apparent 5.1 mph 3B-vs-2B gap is throw CONTEXT and the context-adjusted infield spread is 1.94 mph against a within-position sd of 3.80. TWO ERRORS CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING, both recorded in the gate: (1) the first measurement used data/positional_fit.json (464 rows), which is excluded at deploy/data_exclude.txt:50 and NEVER SERVED; on the real served file (positional_fit_ui.json, 235 rows) coverage is 100% not 99.6%, the Rng+ floor is 80 not 62, 0.0% not 2.4% of rows fall below 80, and there are ZERO catchers, so a prescribed catcher suppression would have been a no-op. (2) The whitelist rule was written as 'CI excludes +0.15', which is also satisfied by a CI lying entirely BELOW +0.15 and therefore literally ADMITS 3B and SS while rejecting 1B; the shipped and tested rule is LOWER BOUND ABOVE +0.15. NOTHING ENTERS THE MODEL: positional_fit.py has no sprint term and does not import the feed (asserted by test_pal_smoke.py source inspection), because OAA already contains the legs and a sprint feature would double-count, the same argument that rejected the arm feature. NOT SHIPPED: any runs-denominated quote (the OF slope is era-unstable, +3.141 OAA/1000inn per ft/s on 2016-2021 against +2.331 on 2022-2026, a 26% swing) and the prospect grade bridge (no MiLB tracking exists anywhere, so a prospect could only get a translation and only 40.2% of active non-pitchers carry a Speed grade). 203 of 235 served rows render a meter; all 203 carry a read.

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07 (Wave B2, X-S1), the starter analog of REM+. Forward-chained OOS 2018-2025 (ex-2020, 702 Y->Y+1 pairs): SEM+ predicts next-year RA9 at rho 0.3923 vs raw FIP 0.358, ERA 0.2612; bootstrap CI on the rho gap beats ERA (lo95 +0.081) and edges its raw-FIP parent (lo95 +0.019), so the empirical-Bayes shrinkage + starter-pool anchoring earn their place. X-S3 'more than FIP' test REJECTED: a ground-ball-adjusted HR expectation (groundOutsToAirouts) scored 0.3905 vs plain 0.3923, gap lo95 -0.0086, so plain FIP stays (starter samples are large enough that observed HR rate is already a strong estimate; loss ledger inside the same artifact). Durability (IP, GS, average start length) is shown as CONTEXT, never in the skill number; quality starts / times-through-order are not in the StatsAPI season feed. Data from the StatsAPI season pitching leaderboard (FanGraphs 403-blocked); no leverage walk (starters are not leverage-deployed). Harness tools/sem_plus_lab.py; core sem_plus.py (reuses the validated rem_plus FIP machinery). models.notes:
2026-08-09/10, preseason base years 2017-2023 at MIN_LAG_YEARS 3, 4,260 pooled common rows deduped to 1,514 players at the latest pre-debut read. THE OWNER QUESTION IS UNANSWERABLE IN MOST CELLS AND NO WEIGHT SHIPS. The global head-to-head does not resolve: d_rho -0.02911 against MDE95 0.03624, bootstrap p 0.1119, winner not_resolvable. 4 of 25 scored cells clear their own MDE95 against 1.25 expected by construction at alpha 0.05, and only 3 survive per-partition Holm (draft_hs -0.07116, RP +0.15578 on n=73, age 23-24 -0.09849); those survivors are largely the SAME PLAYERS seen through three partitions, since a high-school arm is a draft-HS row in a young age bucket. Archetype heterogeneity does not reject one common difference: Cochran Q p 0.2793, label permutation p 0.2629, tau 0.0235, I2 20.5%. All SIX cohort-weight arms lose to equal weight (best archetype_eb_recentre d_rho -0.00021, none clears 0.0068 on Spearman with AUC), random cohort labels do no worse (permutation control p 0.4378 on 200 draws), and the in-sample global oracle gain is 0.00132 on the deduped set and 0.00028 on the A/B pool, both BELOW the ship gate, so estimation error is not the binding constraint: two predictors correlated 0.7134 at similar scale (sd 5.93 vs 5.56) have a nearly flat response surface in the mixing weight, which is geometry and cannot be fixed with more base years. Stated limits carried in the artifact rather than hidden: LEVEL AT GRADING DOES NOT EXIST on this data (snapshots carry no level column) and age at grading is the substitute; the FV-tier cut bins on the consensus, which is a function of both graders, so it is range-restricted and marked scientifically weak; the position-group pitcher cells condition on FanGraphs' own SP/RP designations. Coverage selection is measured, not assumed: 79.1% of rows and 75.1% of players survive the common-set join, and the kept rows run 5.4 FV higher and debut at 0.895 against 0.771. Reproduction is asserted, not claimed: source_backtest is imported and never reimplemented, the six archetype per-source Spearmans reproduce data/source_backtest.json exactly (max abs diff 0.0), and test_source_cohort_accuracy.py pins it. Calibration drift, informational: MLB Pipeline sits 3.29 to 4.19 FV below FanGraphs in every base year, past the 3.0 flag, which is a scale offset the normalization already handles and not an accuracy claim.

models.notes: SHARES THE ARTIFACT with source_cohort_accuracy (block precision_label_free); the registry validator uniques on model_id, and a shared artifact is how a second question measured in one run is registered without inventing a second data/*_eval.json. IDENTIFIED 2026-08-10, superseding this row's earlier 'RAN AND RETURNED UNIDENTIFIED' text, which was written mid-session while the Baseball America boards were still re-ingesting and became false the moment the backfill completed. The row is corrected rather than rewritten silently because a registry row that disagrees with its own artifact is the exact failure this registry exists to catch. EM/FIML on 6,286 rows, non-Heywood, 28 iterations. Patterns: FG+MP 603, FG+MP+BA 3,406, FG+BA 316, MP+BA 220; complete case 3,406, usable at least 2 of 3 4,545, EM leverage 1.334x. sigma FG 3.154 / MP 2.997 / BA 4.808; reliability .655 / .703 / .458; alpha_fg 0.4595, bootstrap CI95 [0.4114, 0.5076]. BASEBALL AMERICA IS MEASURABLY THE NOISIEST of the three, about 60% more grade noise than Pipeline - which is also precisely why it works as the third instrument rather than as a fourth vote. Two sources remain unidentifiable in principle (three second moments against four unknowns); BA is what closes the system. Per-(source, year) centering is REQUIRED: without it BA's variance reads 55.9 instead of 44.7, because a mid-cycle scale rebase reads as variance. GLS weight is w_s proportional to b_s/sigma_s^2, NOT 1/sigma_s^2, which would reward range compression. Sheppard h^2/12 = 2.0833 is reported beside the weight and deliberately NOT subtracted, because the served aggregator observes the quantized grade. PRECISION IS NOT ACCURACY, and the served block still leads with that sentence: this estimator measures how tightly each outlet agrees with the latent consensus once its own scale offset and slope are removed, and says nothing about who is right. On the one cohort where accuracy IS resolvable the two disagree, and precision would have pointed the wrong way. STILL ZERO WEIGHTS SHIP. vintage_availability makes precision estimable only for board years 2023-2026 while the A/B needs Y <= 2023, so the two sets are disjoint and the first year this can be A/B'd is 2027 - structural, not a power problem. NOW CONSUMED DOWNSTREAM: these are the weights B-L6 uses to build its denoised consensus baseline (row efv_denoised_baseline_control, data/xfv_denoised_baseline_eval.json), which read them live from this artifact and re-check the b/sigma^2 identity rather than trusting the stored column. That control found the weights are directionally right and worth only +0.001 rho, against C-A1's own +0.0040 oracle ceiling.

models.notes: Audit 2026-08-07b wave 4, plan lane C4. TWO CORRECTIONS THAT MATTER. (1) THE GATE CURRENCY POINT ESTIMATE IS WITHDRAWN, NOT REPLACED. The first draft of this row installed -$0.117M and a '1.66x understatement' claim; adversarial review blocked it and it is retracted. The lane's PRE-REGISTERED price-ranked instrument points the OTHER WAY (raw_v5 -0.155, raw_v6 -0.135, normalized_v5 -0.158, normalized_v6 -0.134, i.e. v6 makes a rank point worth 13 to 15 percent LESS), the 2x2 was never completed for the served-FV instrument that produced -$0.117M, and the honest range -$0.06M to -$0.17M CONTAINS the published -$0.0704M. So the correct action was to withdraw the point estimate and publish the range, which is what EFV_GATE_STANDARD.md section 4 now does. It is not a conversion rate under any reading: 2.23x spread by segment, opposite signs by instrument, and tie-breaking (-$0.058M) versus cross-grade movement (-$0.232M) inside a single segment. (2) THE PRICING-FLOOR TERM DID NOT GO AWAY, contrary to the plan's expectation that the v6 EV re-fit removed it, but the DIRECTION reported in the first draft of this row was wrong and is corrected here. The lane's own 2x2 reads raw_v5 0.352, raw_v6 0.306, normalized_v5 0.427, normalized_v6 0.385. Holding the FV scale fixed, the v6 calibration makes the share SMALLER on both scales (-13.0 percent raw, -9.7 percent normalized); the headline 0.352 to 0.385 was the DIAGONAL of that table, crossing both factors at once. What survives is that the term is 0.31 to 0.43 in EVERY cell, so it is not gone under any reading, and that it is MISNAMED: 55 to 57 percent of the residual is the TOP realized-WAR quartile being over-priced by +$18.9M to +$25.3M UNDER PERFECT FORESIGHT, which is a pricing-curve problem at the top of the board rather than a floor artifact. It is also the only order-invariant term in the decomposition. FOUR OF SIX CONTROLS FIRED and they bound how far this can be trusted. A NEAR-zero-rank-information board (median FV for everyone, but still carrying age, eta and position through expected_surplus_usd, so 150 distinct prices and Spearman 0.023 against truth, NOT zero-information as first reported) beats the production board on MAE on the v6 frame (11.560 against 12.202) and LOSES on the v5 frame (9.860 against 9.837), and loses on MSE either way. So MAE alone cannot arbitrate a board, but the effect is frame-dependent and was reported one-sided at first. The decomposition is also PATH DEPENDENT (rank/level 0.382/0.232 in one order, 0.712/-0.098 in the other, interaction 0.330) and OBJECTIVE DEPENDENT (level share 0.232 in MAE against 0.032 in MSE, a 7x disagreement, indistinguishable from zero under the EV-consistent loss). Quote the shares only with the order and the objective attached.

The 2026-07-01 artifact priced the retired $13,025,154 per WAR level (re-anchor scale 1.1095) while the board priced $17,143,641 (scale 1.4603), and it dated itself under the bare key generated, which model_registry did not read, so this row aged by file mtime and read not stale at 90 days while the artifact's own stamp said 92. The 2026-07-01 structural facts below (FV<=40 level-invariant, isotonic amplification up to about 1.9x, about 3,300 players pinned at a 1.44M floor) described the retired level and pricing path and are RETIRED.

HISTORY (2026-07-01 run, retired level; every number in it is superseded): Holistic pass 3 (2026-07-01). Ordering is level-invariant: zero top-50 churn at every shift, max top-50 move 2 spots (-20% only), FV45+ rho >=0.9999 everywhere; dollar levels move roughly with the shift (FV60+ median +24% at +20%). Structural facts recorded: FV<=40 (3,491 players) is level-invariant by design (fixed-dollar low-tier anchor is not market-indexed); the isotonic output layer amplifies level shifts up to ~1.9x in FV 45-50 and pins ~3,300 players at the 1.44M floor.
