models.notes: MASTER PLAN 2026-07-30 PHASE 4 (LANE-TOOLS). Gates pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/TOOL_GRADE_TABLES.md section 1 BEFORE the first table was fitted. Verdict is `provisional` in the registry's own sense (measured, but descriptive-only correlation): these are measurement tables, not a forecaster, and nothing forward was gated. HEADLINE: our measured tool curves are FLATTER than every published table at every tool in both contexts; measured SD per 10 grade points is 0.84-0.97 for fastball velocity and only 0.43-0.67 for the hitting tools, so the FanGraphs 10-points-is-one-SD claim survives only where we measure the quantity precisely (the ratio is a lower bound; per-player sampling noise inflates the denominator). AUDIT CELLS: fastball velocity confirms Baseball America and refutes the FanGraphs 2014 column as stale (our SP 50 = 93.0 mph, BA 93, FG 90-91; BA exact at 50/55/65, FG cold by 1.6-2.5 at all four auditable cells). Game power disagrees with BA at 55 in all three frames and at 60 in two of three (the age-26 60 cell has n=24 and a CI too wide to separate) by 4.9-9.3 HR while agreeing with FanGraphs at both, and reverses at 40/50 where BA is closer: BA's home-run-era recentring over-corrected at the top. Hit tool: FanGraphs and BA agree with each other (framework doc X4 control holds) and both are hot above 50. Smith W2's stolen-base table survives at 50 and 60; his UZR/150 and Fld/3 tables are hot (a 50 field grade measures -0.25 runs, not +1.5, which vindicates Smith's own flagged qualified-population caveat); his SP and RP control tables are too steep above 50. Published adjustments tested at matched grade: the 1 mph left-hander deduction CONFIRMED at 1.19 mph, the 1-2 mph reliever addition measures only 0.59 mph and is reported as a lower bound because our role split is realized MLB usage. NO MEASUREMENT (findings, not gaps): throw/arm, pitch_sel, bat_ctrl (the Savant minors bat_speed column is empty in every row), delivery, athl, frame; speed is proxy-only because no sprint speed, 60-yard or home-to-first time exists anywhere in the tree, so both published speed tables (seconds) are unauditable. Context handled within player: AAA minus MLB exit velocity is -0.06 mph (CI -0.23 to +0.12, n 422), so the upper-minors EV table reads on the MLB scale directly; every other quantity carries a measured offset on its row. INVENTIONS, each pre-registered: INV-1 measurement-implied tool grade PASSES on 9 of 13 tool-context cells and fails 4 on flag rate because compressed bands make the inverse ill-conditioned; INV-2 per-source drift index finds MLB Pipeline's tool grades run hot vs FanGraphs' on EVERY tool in both contexts on paired players (fb -3.35, hit -2.54, speed -2.50, field -2.33, game_pwr -1.47 grade points in the MLB context, fb -3.89 and hit -3.69 in the upper minors, every CI excluding zero), and Baseball America is NOT COMPUTABLE because BA contributes zero tool grades across the whole 2011-2026 snapshot history; INV-3 per-tool grade aging is descriptive and list-retention confounded (contact and command grades decay, power grades rise). NONE of the three is wired into consensus weighting or eFV scoring; each needs its own accuracy gate. Lab tools/tool_grade_tables_lab.py (offline, read-only, --write to regenerate).

models.notes:
FIRST outcome validation of the Trade Machine (previously only 55 policy/invariant tests, unregistered). Slice A (n=2333 resolved players, xfv.realized_war = full career bWAR, RANK only): board surplus orders realized WAR about as well as raw consensus FV pooled (Spearman 0.329 vs 0.331) and ranks 'useful MLB asset' well (AUC 0.771, hitters 0.383 > pitchers 0.301), BUT does NOT beat consensus FV within tiers (won 1/4: elite 0.151 vs 0.323, high 0.150 vs 0.219, mid 0.086 vs 0.271, low 0.084 vs 0.067) -> ship=False, FLAGGED. Slice A' (per surplus_source, exercises the apply_platform_surplus join): projection-source (surNpv) Spearman vs CAREER WAR is ~0 (0.016) - EXPECTED, surNpv is a forward 5-yr NPV for vets, not a career-WAR predictor (unit mismatch); xfv_backgrade 0.213. HONEST: not a forward backtest (TM values were never snapshotted), uses current grades on already-graduated players (survivorship+hindsight), career-vs-control-window unit mismatch -> proves ORDERING only, never live trade-price accuracy; it inherits xFV (provisional) + projections validity. Verdict stays provisional until a forward cohort accrues - START snapshotting trade_values.json now. Slice B (bounded-window calibration via surplus_backtest_real) is the documented next extension. Built tools/trade_machine_backtest.py. WITHIN-TIER ORDERING (2026-06-25): the audit found the convex-$/WAR + $0-floor surplus transform COMPRESSES within-tier ordering - the raw xfv_grade it is derived from orders realized WAR better in every tier (elite 0.233 vs surplus 0.149, high 0.249 vs 0.151, mid 0.254 vs 0.082) and pooled (0.343 vs 0.329); ~33% of resolved players bunch at <=$0.5M with no internal order. Board now carries xfv_grade and TIE-BREAKS on it within equal surplus (orders the floored block sensibly); the eval reports it as xfv_grade_orderer. Display value + headline sort stay the $ surplus, so the ship gate (surplus vs consensus, career-WAR rank) is unchanged (ship still False) and the verdict stays provisional - the true call awaits the forward backtest (snapshotting TBD). SNAPSHOTTING STARTED (2026-06-25): new storage.snapshot_trade_values + trade_value_history table, wired into run_monthly step 6d, captures each board record's surplus value as-of date. This is the INSTRUMENT the provisional verdict was waiting on - a TRUE forward backtest (as-of-T trade_value_mm vs realized bWAR accrued in (T, T+k], per surplus_source, vs the as-of-T consensus baseline) becomes possible once a few months accrue, removing the survivorship+hindsight caveat. Cannot be back-filled; the track record begins now. H-1 (2026-07-05): the Trade Machine board and the PROSPX trade board now rank by xfv_grade (the eFV grade the surplus is derived from) instead of trade_value_mm - the eval shows grade orders realized WAR better (rho 0.3433 vs surplus 0.3289 POOLED, with no interval and no floor) and in the elite, high and mid tiers, but LOSES in the low tier (0.0683 against 0.0816). CORRECTED 2026-09-06: this note said grade wins within EVERY tier, and the eval's own by_tier block contradicts that on the low tier, which holds 1,301 of the 2,333 scored rows and is larger than the other three combined; the Surplus column still sorts by $ and $ values still display. This is the approved within-tier mitigation, not a claim the surplus predictor itself ships (ship=false stands). SUPER-TWO LADDER FIX (2026-07-16, correctness recalibration, not an accuracy claim): the legacy super_two_first_fraction 0.25 (calibrated for the 0.40/0.60/0.80 arb ladder) was prepended unchanged onto the clemens_2026 0.15/0.35/0.50/0.75 schedule, pricing a super-two's first arb year ABOVE his second (non-monotone). Fixed in value_framework._arb_ladder: the prepended fraction is clamped to the schedule's arb-1 step (min(configured, fracs[0])), monotone by construction under every valuation set; single source for the prospect, remaining and consumed paths. prospx_current output is byte-identical (0.25 < 0.40 passes through). Effect under clemens_2026 (22% population blend): super-two salaries fall, surplus rises slightly (50 FV hitter 18.5 -> 18.6 $M). No new empirical estimate of super-two award levels is claimed; the clemens sources publish none. Artifacts re-emitted via value_framework.py --emit-snapshots.

2026-08-19 reading: FIRST forward_backtest (instrument maturation, NO win claims) off the trade_value_history snapshots started 2026-06-25: 43 snapshot dates through 2026-08-19, 254,341 rows. S1 30d value-stability Spearman 0.5990, player-clustered bootstrap 95% CI [0.5833, 0.6145] (B=1000, seed 20260819), n=122,808 pairs / 5,975 players / 22 origin dates: MODERATE stability, not high; real churn, and the pooled window spans the trade deadline (origins 2026-06-25..07-25). S2 movement signal NULL by the pre-committed reading: observed rho -0.2635 (abs rho 0.2635) does NOT exceed the within-date shuffle control band (abs rho p97.5 = 0.6335; the mechanical -value(T) coupling stays in the null), so no evidence surplus predicts short-horizon movement; NOT evidence trade values are wrong; expected at 30d. S3 coverage: 22 of 43 origin dates pair at [25,35]d nearest-30, retention 0.9913, only drop = 1,073 player-absent-at-T2 rows, zero NULLs. Results live in the forward_backtest block of data/trade_machine_eval.json; all 7 pre-existing keys preserved value-identical and the previously empty generated_at now reads 2026-08-19; ship stays false. Gate doc docs/trade-2026-08-19/TRADE_FORWARD_GATE.md; lab tools/trade_value_forward_backtest.py (refuses <2 snapshot dates). Re-run when 60-90d horizons become poolable (~late September 2026).

A different label is a different definition, not a gain in accuracy (gate clause (l)).

models.notes:
the template: distributionally validated, auto-propagates recalibrations || DEMOTED validated -> provisional 2026-09-04 (audit F27, F46). The row claimed 'PIT uniformity + coverage' against data/value_framework_fitted.json, and that artifact contains NO WAG EVIDENCE. Scanned 2026-09-04, its top-level keys are bayes, bucket_midpoints, empirical_anchors, framework_version, generated_by, method, parallel_lines_diagnostic, per_threshold, proportional_odds, reconciliation, training_n; the substrings 'wag', 'coverage' and 'uniform' occur ZERO times in the whole file. What it does hold is the fitted FV -> WAR bucket curve (generated_by `value_framework.py --fit`, framework_version v2.0, training_n hitter 678 / pitcher 437) that WAG differences against, so the pointer is kept as PROVENANCE for the baseline curve and is not evidence for the residual metric. A REALIZED-PIT ARTIFACT DOES NOT EXIST: the only PIT test on record samples outcomes from the model itself (audit F27), which cannot falsify the model. Two adjacent findings bound what a real one has to fix before it can be run. F24: the engine WAG baseline is bust-inclusive, so a graduate is scored against an expectation containing outcomes impossible for him (at FV 45 with P(bust) 0.505 an exactly average survivor reads PIT 0.636, against a realized settled-graduate mean of 0.560 with boom/bust shares 24.5 / 7.8 percent on a 20/20 design); the coherent baseline is E[WAR | FV, debuted, exposure]. F26: exposure is counted in calendar seasons at a full 600 PA / 200 IP each while the median real load is 0.31 of a season, and 769 of 1,580 settled rows record zero MLB PA or IP that a `pa or None` seam converts into 'unknown'. NOTHING SERVED MOVES with this demotion: verdict and prose only. || RE-POINTED 2026-09-11 (owner decisions 14b and 14c). models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-29 (Phase G of the 2026-07-29 master plan). Convention 3 of docs/efv-2026-07-29/ARKMETRIC_SCALE_CONVENTIONS.md: 100 + 10z, ten points per anchor-pool standard deviation, measured at exactly 10.0 on all three pools in the live-season scale check inside data/war_rate_plus_eval.json. A ratio-to-mean index is UNDEFINED on this rate (league mean WAR/PA is +0.0025 and individual values go negative), so there is deliberately no HEM_SPREAD_GAIN analog; the index is a single leg z-scored against its own pool, so nothing needs re-standardizing. WAR source is the served provider (eWAR v2 through war_source, the same series for the 1-year column and, since the 2026-09-11 re-point, for the lab and the 3-year column; bWAR before that) with the batting and pitching sides read from SEPARATE keys (mlb_player_export._war_daily shape); fa_projection._war_age_maps is banned here because it sums the sides and would divide a two-way player's pitching WAR by his plate appearances. Two-way players carry two indexes on two boards with two denominators and need no discount factor. A degenerate WAR fetch is REFUSED rather than served as a board of zeros (the fa_projection.py:191-201 pattern), pinned by test_war_rate_plus.py. No shrink and no clamp (true-to-model policy). SEPARATE METRIC from war_ip_plus_sp by design (ARKMETRIC_SCALE_CONVENTIONS.md:77), never one pooled column. Anchor pool relievers with 20+ IP; display gate 30 IP (40 IP was rejected: it leaves only 95 arms at midseason). Live 2026 board: 171 of 454 rows stamped off a 227-row pool, displayed spread 9.8 points. Unlike REM+ this is NOT leverage-blind by construction, because bWAR prices the runs actually prevented; the gmLI / WPA / SD-MD columns still carry deployment separately, and REM+ stays the leverage-free talent number. FORWARD GATE, run and LOST, reported honestly. G1 passes on all three pools: each index beats a zero-information control by a wide margin (hitters gap lo95 +0.3183, starters +0.1365, relievers +0.0233), so these carry real signal. G2 (beat the best naive baseline at predicting next season's WAR rate) FAILS on all three: hitters 0.3711 vs plain season bWAR 0.4058 (n 3845, gap lo95 -0.0479, a resolvable loss), starters 0.2688 vs 0.2799 (n 1396, lo95 -0.0307, CI spans zero), relievers 0.0886 vs 0.0899 (n 1621, lo95 -0.0145, CI spans zero). Mechanism: a season of playing time is itself a talent signal and a per-trip rate throws it away. Harness tools/plus_lab_harness.py v2 with the convention PRE-DECLARED as v2 (within-outcome-season z target, player-clustered season-stratified bootstrap, complete-outcome-season pairs only, unrounded predictors, no imputation); v1 rides alongside and agrees. Lab tools/war_rate_plus_lab.py. Measurement ledger data/war_rate_plus_eval.json, carried on this row's notes rather than as eval_artifact because the row is honestly unvalidated and model_registry.validate() forbids an unvalidated row from holding an artifact. Relievers forward-predict weakly on BOTH arms here (0.089), which is the same volatility the REM+ gate measured when it landed at 0.236 against an easier target. SHRINK: pre-registered NO, and the arm was measured. Arm S (regress the rate toward the pool by sample size, mu/sd taken from the SHRUNK pool so the aStuff+ C3 defect class is avoided by construction) CLEARED its pre-registered lo95 > 0 bar on hitters (+0.0100) and relievers (+0.0002) and not on starters (-0.0014). The ship is UNSHRUNK anyway, which is an override of the rule as written and is argued in the shrink_ruling block of data/war_rate_plus_eval.json rather than assumed: shrinking changes what the column MEANS (at the display gate the published number would be about 70 percent league average, so war/pa on the same row would no longer reproduce the index), the gain sits at or under this repo's own noise floor, it collapses inside predictor-volume terciles (a post-hoc control, labelled as such: within-band gains of +0.0029 or less, clearing zero in one of nine bands), and G2 failed so the shipped surface makes no forward claim to optimise. OWNER CALL OPEN: shipping shrunk is a registered, measured candidate. Reader-facing methodology: glossary entries war_ip_plus_rp and war_ip_plus_rp_3yr. COMPANION COLUMN ADDED 2026-07-30: `war_ip_plus_adj` serves the same rate regressed toward the pool rate by sample size (K = pool median denominator) and re-standardised ON THE SHRUNK POOL, so it is still exactly ten points per sigma. This closes the owner_call recorded OPEN in the ledger's shrink_ruling: the pre-registered arm-S rule had fired on hit and RP and the ship stayed unshrunk. The owner's ruling was ship it, but as a SEPARATE column, because an adjusted value no longer reproduces war/denominator on the row and reusing the raw name would silently change what a published number means. Verdict is UNCHANGED and still `unvalidated`: G2 failed on every pool, and the volume control shows the shrink gain is mostly a volume leak, so the companion is a readability aid and not a forward claim. Decision record: docs/efv-2026-07-30/WAR_RATE_SHRINK_OWNER_CALL.md. A 1yr percentile chip (`war_ip_plus_pct`, midrank over served rows) ships alongside it so a 10-points-per-sigma value can be read as rarity without z arithmetic. RE-POINTED 2026-09-11 (audit F10-01, owner decision): the lab now reads the served WAR provider (eWAR v2, FIP re-priced within role) instead of pybaseball's bWAR files, so the ledger measures the series the column serves. 2026-09-11 reading, SUPERSEDING the reliever figures above: n 1621, index 0.2323 against season WAR 0.2267 (gap lo95 -0.0081) and the same rate left unstandardized 0.2319 (gap lo95 -0.0033), a tie with both, so G2 still FAILS and the row stays unvalidated; G1 lo95 +0.1574; arm S NO LONGER fires on this pool (gap 0.002, lo95 -0.0016; the _adj companion stays by the 2026-07-30 owner ruling, as a readability aid); G4 3yr 0.2590 vs 1yr 0.2323, lo95 -0.0035, now UNRESOLVED.

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-29 alongside war_pa_plus / war_ip_plus_sp / war_ip_plus_rp. FROZEN VINTAGE, not pipeline output: the three exporters read the values VERBATIM from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json (three blocks, hit / sp / rp, because the three anchor pools are three metrics) and never recompute them, so a board row can show a same-day 1-year value beside a 3-year value frozen weeks earlier. Each board payload carries a multiyear_war_rate vintage block (generated_at, season, window, anchor_pool, n_in_artifact) plus the explicit disclosure that the value is as of generated_at and NOT as of the board's as_of date; players who joined the pool after the lab ran are blank, and a provisional tag prints a star. Established needs 2+ seasons and 600 PA / 120 IP (starters) / 40 IP (relievers) in the window, mirroring hem_plus_3yr / sem_plus_3yr / rem_plus_3yr. A contributing season must clear the DISPLAY gate, not just the pool floor, so the 3-year column is a mean of values the board would actually publish and a player cannot hold a 3-year value while his 1-year cell is blank. Artifact holds 615 hitters, 282 starters, 443 relievers for the 2024-2026 window. HISTORY (2026-06 to 2026-08, retained so the retirement is legible rather than silent):
LEAN FV-as-prior + earned adjustments (OBP, K-rate, age-vs-level, n_milb_seasons track-record, hit/speed tools; power deliberately omitted = power-correction), shipped as a guarded blend (lam=0.9 toward consensus, WAG-calibrated). STRUCTURAL alternatives also tested + REJECTED 2026-06-22 (forward-chained, same folds): two-part P(MLB)xE(WAR|MLB) (marginal full-pool Spearman, costs AUC, ties flagship), monotonic LightGBM + ridge/GBM stack (worse on hitter flagship 0.30/0.32 vs 0.33 -- overfits at n~400/cohort), confidence-weighted shrinkage toward consensus (no change). Conclusion: ridge is at the DATA'S rank ceiling; further gains need NEW data (historical Statcast/Stuff+, which we lack pre-~2023), not more modeling. The misses are irreducible variance (xFV right on 53% of its disagreements w/ consensus). CONDITIONAL POWER also REJECTED 2026-06-22 (the Bobby-Witt power-star miss): realized-in-games power, level-weighted (iso_x_level/iso_upper/peak_iso_x_level) + contact-paired (iso_x_hit/iso_x_contact), all FAILED OOS (best debuted-km -0.0016; replacing tool_speed cost -0.014) -- third independent confirmation (raw iso -> peak iso -> conditional) that game power does not earn a place; the power-star miss is the accepted cost of the population-level power-overpricing correction. THRESHOLD-GATED POWER + CREATIVE COHORT-SLICING also REJECTED 2026-06-22 (per-year-robustness gate added: a pooled pass only counts if positive in >=3/4 forward-chained folds): hit/obp/contact-gated power (iso_gh50/55/60, iso_gobp, iso_gk, pwrtool_gh55, double-gates) = 4th power rejection (best stack +0.0036 pooled but NEGATIVE in 2022+2023 = a 2020-21 artifact); level-weighted production (obp_x_level/k_x_level/obp_upper, add+replace) rejected; 23 creative slices (FV-tier mid-band, age-band x production, up-the-middle x production, breakout prod_trend x level, reliability/exposure weighting, source-disagreement + safe-floor composites) all rejected -- every pooled-passer was a 2020-21 fold artifact that reverses on the freshest cohorts (the level_rank/milb_missing data-vintage fingerprint). HIGH-END TAIL FIX REJECTED (2026-06-25, owner asked 'can a tail fix improve xFV at the high end, ex. Bobby Witt Jr.'): NO - committed as a loss. Forward-chained diagnosis (tools/xfv_tail_lab.py, the SAME OOS protocol as this eval) shows the top tier is already OVER-predicted vs realized first-6yr WAR, not under: FV>=55 hitters predict 10.4 vs realized 7.7 (bias +2.7), pitchers 6.0 vs 3.5 (bias +2.5) - a winner's-curse/attrition artifact that is INVISIBLE in-sample, so no correction fit on train transfers to it. Tested forward-chained, all LOSSES, none shipped: tail expansion (worsens FV55+ calibration), tail compression (no transfer - collapses to identity), global per-fold linear recalibration (worsens FV55+ MAE/bias - it is MSE-optimal for the bulk, not the bimodal tail), high-FV prior-anchoring lambda dip (rank delta hit -0.001 / pit +0.0002 = noise). models.notes: Audit 2026-08-07b lane B1. VERDICT MATERIAL_BIAS: the projection UNDER-states at every span, monotone, negative on both sides. hit -1.691 CI95[-2.091,-1.267] and pit -0.839 [-1.169,-0.522] at n_obs=2, decaying to null at n_obs=5 (hit -0.062 [-0.168,+0.043]). Mechanism confirmed independently by a second route: seasons 4-6 carry 59.60 percent of six-year WAR mass, so projecting flat from the first two seasons recovers only 64.7 percent of the truth, and that ratio predicts the per-magnitude-bin bias to within about 0.5 WAR. 833 shipped rows ride the projection (hit 382, pit 451). NARROWED BY ADVERSARIAL REVIEW and the narrowing is the honest reading: only n2_hit is material under the lane's own rule (n2_pit clears significance but not materiality), and a single rescale constant collapses the magnitude ladder from (-2.547/-4.516/-7.032) to (-0.856/-0.687/-1.035), so the top-bin figure is the pooled bias expressed at a higher level rather than incremental top-end damage. Multiplicity uncorrected across 48 nested strata. DOWNSTREAM, which is why this artifact matters beyond its own lane: 30.26 percent of rows change realized outcome bucket at n_obs=2, 198 down against 101 up (two to one pessimistic). That is the SAME SIGN as the D3 reliability miscalibration and is the reason lane C1 must not recalibrate against the censored bucket. The star-AUC positive class (WAR>=10) loses 40 percent of its true positives at n_obs=2. NO MODEL CHANGE SHIPPED: a replacement label needs its own gate doc, a rank-identical level twin, a random-label null band and a permutation p-value. Doc docs/efv-2026-08-07b/LABEL_CENSORING_GATE.md. (Wave H rebuilt-matrix re-select artifact data/xfv_wave_h_eval.json) CITATION CORRECTED 2026-08-07: this sentence was duplicated with data/xfv_surplus_recal_eval.json in place of the wave-H path, which was a copy-paste from the 07-25 baseline. That file is the B1 surplus calibration ledger (lane 'B1 surplus calibration -> accuracy', verdict SHIP linear0, zero lambda content) and it is cited on prospect_surplus, where it belongs; it was never a lambda re-select artifact.

RE-SWEPT 2026-08-07 on the 11-fold pair-weighted basis, one sweep per side, grid 0.35 to 0.90 across the clamp (data/xfv_driver_lambda_sweep.json, docs/efv-drivers-2026-08-07/GATE_RECORD.md section 8). NEITHER SERVED PIN MOVES. Both curves are monotone decreasing in lambda over the entire grid, so each argmax is the grid edge, which is also the _BLEND_LAMBDA_CLAMP floor: hit 0.70 -> 0.35 is +0.00522 at 0.27x its floor with CI95 [-0.0033, +0.0430]; pit 0.57 -> 0.40 is +0.00286 at 0.27x with CI95 [-0.0042, +0.0216]. Both CIs straddle zero, which is precisely what the reopening rule at efv_model.py:480-483 exists to refuse. The whole hitter band spans 0.0079 in pooled rho and the whole pitcher band 0.0160, so on hitters the entire admissible lambda range is smaller than a single feature-add floor. THE BLOCK-RHO LEG DISAGREES WITH THE POOLED LEG ON HITTERS and is the reason not to read the monotone curve as a finding: hitter block-rho over the grid is flat and non-monotone (0.4014 at 0.35, 0.4002 at 0.70, 0.4011 at 0.60), so 'less model weight is better' is an artifact of between-fold level differences that block-normalization removes; on pitchers the two legs do agree. Churn cost quoted as the reopening rule requires: moving hit 0.70 to 0.35 would re-blend and re-print every hitter grade on the board and halve the model's weight in the headline, for a 0.27x-floor claim that one of the two required instruments does not support, and the 0.85-to-0.70 precedent was itself taken on churn grounds and explicitly NOT as an accuracy claim. Recorded beside the elite-band result (xfv_elite_band): the owner's conviction ask wants MORE model trust at the top and this sweep's own argmax wants LESS model trust everywhere, both sub-floor, and the eval cannot tell the two opposite prescriptions apart. Lambda-shift floors re-derived in the same run: 0.0025 hit / 0.0030 pit for a 0.05 shift and 0.0046 / 0.0055 for a 0.10 shift (data/xfv_driver_floors.json), far tighter than the retired 0.0076-0.011 / 0.005-0.008 and scaling with the size of the shift, which the old single number hid. Lambda is genuinely the one gate class the 11-fold promotion made MORE resolvable.

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-31 after clearing its pre-registration on EVERY condition. THE DEFECT: p_bucket_given_fv is fitted on the CONSENSUS-FV scale (sd 6.57 on the served-comparable pool) and read in production at the realized-implied eFV grade (sd 15.54), 2.4x wider, so its log-odds came out about 2.7x too steep. That is a SLOPE error, which is why per-cohort intercept offsets could never have fixed it. GATE, all on held-out forward-chained folds (6 splits, 1,740 pooled rows): beats the INCUMBENT on Brier +0.030139 CI95 [+0.021109,+0.039055] and log loss +0.091055 CI95 [+0.065310,+0.116788]; beats a CONSTANT base rate on Brier +0.031369 CI95 [+0.026449,+0.035966] and log loss +0.101815 CI95 [+0.085284,+0.117593]. All four CIs clean of zero, which is the bar TWO prior odds lanes failed. Label-shuffle zero-information control (200 refits on permuted labels): null CI95 [-0.006157,+0.003907] against an observed +0.030139, p=0.0 on both metrics. Monotone in the input probability, so it cannot reorder anything. MECHANISM CONFIRMED, which the gate required and not just the score: calibration slope 0.6446 -> 1.1351 and ECE 0.1528 -> 0.0428. NOTE the gate text predicted the slope would move 'from 0.368'; that figure came from the 517-row subpool used in the cohort lane's refutation, and on this 1,740-row frame the incumbent slope is 0.6446. Both are real and they are different populations; the direction claim held and the starting value is reported as measured. HONEST CAVEAT: F LOSES fold 2015 on Brier (0.1887 against 0.1672), which is the first fold carrying a Platt arm and so the one with the least history to fit on. It wins 5 of 6 against the incumbent and 6 of 6 against the constant. BLAST RADIUS, measured: 9,320 of 9,334 served p_bust values moved, 8,073 by more than 5 points (5,743 down, 2,330 up); every p_bucket vector still sums to 1; and ZERO rows changed xfv_grade, xfv_grade_quantile, xfv_war_6yr or surplus_mm, so no rank, grade or dollar figure moved. Brayden Taylor p_bust 0.309 -> 0.605 and Enrique Bradfield Jr 0.319 -> 0.609, most of the way to the 77.1% bust rate of their own outcome-comp cohort, reached with ZERO cohort information. THE CODE ALREADY EXISTED: efv_odds_calibration.py was written 2026-07-25 and left inert with an exact wiring patch at tools/_prem_odds.patch; this lane independently re-derived the finding under a fresh pre-registration and then wired it. A DEFECT IN THAT PATCH WAS FOUND AND FIXED while wiring: its backgrade hunk gated on `not rec.get('milb')`, but debuts.json rows carry no milb block at all (measured: 0 of 2,676), so the expression was always True and would have silently disabled the correction for the entire resolved population. That is backwards, because the resolved frame is exactly what the map was fit on. The guard is kept on the two seams where an absent milb block genuinely means no MiLB track record, and dropped on the backgrade seam. SISTER LANE: the cohort rebuild that chased the same Taylor and Bradfield complaint directly was a measured NO-SHIP, killed by its own zero-information control, with cohort conditioning going NEGATIVE on a calibrated base (data/xfv_odds_cohort_eval.json).

Shuffling reproduces the entire gain, so the cohort information contributes nothing. THE MOTIVATING AXIS WAS ALSO FIT and also fails: the first pass tested only age_rel_level grids, but the motivating cells are cut on ABSOLUTE age (archetype_comps facets.age edges 20/22/23.5); fitted, level x ABS-AGE x sign gives d_inc_brier +0.007831 CI [-0.001055,+0.018863], CI includes zero. THE HYPOTHESIS IS INVERTED BY THE DATA: the gain is strictly DECREASING in cell count (1 cell +0.0222, 2 +0.0198, 4 +0.0139, 8 +0.0119, 19 +0.0093, 33 +0.0078, 35 +0.0078), and a ONE-cell grid carries no cohort information at all yet beats the 33-cell pre-registered grid by 2.8x on Brier and 6.5x on log loss. ROOT CAUSE, which is why the design could never have worked: the incumbent calibration SLOPE is 0.368 with ECE 0.201, and a per-cohort logit OFFSET can only move the intercept. Fit a global Platt (2 params, zero cohort info) and cohort offsets on top go NEGATIVE (d_brier -0.000709, d_logloss -0.008411): cohorts only ever looked useful because they were absorbing miscalibration that two global parameters absorb better. CORRECTION TO THE FIRST PASS, recorded so it does not enter the ledger as fact: the first pass proposed to describe this as the identical beats_incumbent-true / beats_constant-false signature as xfv_odds_recalibration_ship. That is FALSE. That artifact records d_const_brier +0.013289 and d_const_logloss +0.041014, both POSITIVE; it beat the constant on point estimate and failed on CI width and the permutation null. Different failure in kind. The first pass also charged the candidate with a log-loss loss to the constant that PRE-EXISTS it (the raw incumbent loses by -0.063613 on the same 517 rows; the cohort head improves that to -0.056561). HONEST CONCLUSION PUBLISHED: our bust odds are calibrated to the GRADE and not to the player, and conditioning on cohort does not fix it; readers wanting the 24-year-old-repeating-AAA answer should use the outcome-comp cohorts directly, which already carry 77.1 percent. SPUN OUT, NOT SHIPPED: the Platt row is a real finding this lane was not chartered to make and it clears the hard bar (+0.049776 Brier / +0.102545 log loss against a constant); pre-registered separately at docs/efv-2026-07-30/ODDS_CALIBRATION_SLOPE_GATE.md rather than shipped on a gate written for a different hypothesis.

models.notes: LANE-ODDS, owner decision 2026-07-30 'measure before deciding'. Pre-registration written to disk BEFORE any measurement: docs/efv-2026-07-30/ODDS_GRADE_BASIS_GATE.md PART 1. Follows the LANE-P2 pin (docs/efv-2026-07-30/POOLED_OUTCOME_REFIT.md section 1.3). VERDICT: KEEP THE PIN, and the split is now a measured choice rather than an unexamined leftover. The re-key FAILS criterion 1 (not better on both metrics on both sides: pitchers Brier +0.0294 / log loss +0.0782 WORSE, hitters a null) and the pooled paired bootstrap CI95 excludes zero with the PIN ahead (Brier d -0.01375 CI [-0.01998,-0.00651], log loss d -0.02964 CI [-0.04762,-0.00901], P(re-key better) 0.000 / 0.002; sign convention d = pin - re-key). 13 of 14 side-folds favour the pin; the single exception is hitters 2014, the thinnest fold, where both arms lose to a constant. THE SHIFT IS LEVEL, NOT CALIBRATION, on four independent lines: AUC identical (0.8193 vs 0.8193 hit, 0.7828 vs 0.7833 pit); Murphy resolution identical (0.0395 vs 0.0404, 0.0177 vs 0.0175) with the whole Brier gap in the RELIABILITY term (0.0674->0.0700, 0.0334->0.0633); the rank-identical twins reproduce each arm to 4dp (twin-with-pin-marginal 0.14077 vs pin 0.14080, twin-with-rekey-marginal 0.15885 vs re-key 0.15879); and the decile reliability curve's OBSERVED column does not move at all, only the PREDICTED column, downward through deciles 4-7 where observed bust is already 0.90-0.97. The secondary served-comparable cut (n=516) flips sign nominally in the re-key's favour, and does NOT overturn this: it reverses after out-of-fold Platt recalibration (pooled_served Brier d -0.00546, log loss d -0.02890 CI [-0.08145,-0.00071]) and its observed delta sits BELOW its own permutation null band (+0.0091 observed vs null [+0.0185,+0.0308] Brier; +0.0413 vs [+0.0981,+0.1403] log loss). Pre-registration on disk and committed BEFORE the lab was written or run: docs/efv-2026-07-30/ODDS_INDEX_MISMATCH_GATE.md PART 1. THE MISMATCH IS REAL AND NOW HAS NUMBERS. p_bucket_given_fv is a proportional-odds fit on five published CONSENSUS-FV cells per side (value_framework_config.yaml:63-77; training_n 678 hit / 437 pit) whose own recorded support is data/value_framework_fitted.json bayes.data_fv_range = [45, 60]. Production evaluates it at realized_implied_fv(model WAR), which on the resolved out-of-fold frame has mean 37.00 sd 15.26 (hit) and 35.66 sd 10.15 (pit) against a consensus marginal of 42.24 sd 5.66 and 41.52 sd 4.50: 2.70x and 2.26x the dispersion the curve was fitted for, 5.2 to 5.9 FV low on the mean. A SECOND mismatch nobody had stated is larger: 65% to 84% of every column sits BELOW the fitted support, the consensus column included, so the table is read outside its range on most rows no matter which scale indexes it. (Two figures in the brief do not reproduce and are corrected in 1.1; the direction and magnitude class are confirmed.) VERDICT: FIXING THE UNITS IS A NULL. The candidate fails the owner's criterion on BOTH required cuts. Pooled it fails with the CI excluding zero in the WRONG direction: vs the flat constant, Brier d = -0.02083 CI95 [-0.03974,-0.00716] P(cand)=0.001 and log loss d = -0.06599 CI95 [-0.11610,-0.03014] P=0.001. On pooled_served the point estimates favour it (+0.03538 / +0.06322) but neither interval excludes zero (CI95 [-0.00727,+0.06996] P=0.932; [-0.04710,+0.15074] P=0.831). THE DECISIVE DIAGNOSTIC settles the attribution: on the pooled frame the table read at its NATIVE consensus-FV index ALSO loses to the flat constant (Brier d = -0.01399 CI95 [-0.02778,+0.00035]; log loss d = -0.04465 CI95 [-0.07921,-0.00875] P=0.006), while on the served-comparable cut the same curve in the same units BEATS it decisively (Brier +0.05656 CI95 [+0.02281,+0.08929] P=1.000; log loss +0.12145 CI95 [+0.04692,+0.19895] P=0.999, both far above their permutation null bands). So the INDEX is exonerated and the POPULATION is convicted: this is a model of a published-list cohort (Clemens 2025, 51-53% bust at FV45) scored on the whole eFV matrix (84-88% bust), and no change of argument crosses a base-rate gap of thirty-five points. That is why re-indexing moves the level the wrong way (calibration-in-the-large -0.1533 to -0.2411) and why the 2026-07-25 recalibration moved only the level. WHAT DOES SURVIVE, registered and NOT recommended: the consensus-scale keying carries genuinely MORE information than the incumbent keying. Pooled AUC 0.8289 vs 0.7967, Murphy resolution 0.0311 vs 0.0273, and the level-shift trap does NOT fire - after out-of-fold Platt recalibration of both arms the candidate still wins, pooled Brier +0.01003 CI95 [+0.00300,+0.02144] P=0.997 and log loss +0.03746 CI95 [+0.01717,+0.07518] P=0.999, both above their null bands (hitter-driven; pitchers are a null). Contrast the re-key of xfv_odds_grade_basis, whose AUC was identical to the incumbent's to three decimals. Acting on this would mean stacking the candidate on a recalibration that is itself a measured NULL against a base rate, so it is not assembled here. The variant on pure model WAR instead of the consensus-guarded rank_war (QWAR) is uniformly slightly worse, so the consensus information in rank_war is doing part of the work. PER SPLIT: only 3 of 7 folds favour the candidate on Brier and the two heaviest losses are the two largest folds, which are also the two with the highest bust base rates. PROVENANCE: the lab reproduces the basis gate's incumbent (pooled Brier 0.14080, log loss 0.46089 vs published 0.14080 / 0.46088) and the ship gate's recalibrated arm (0.11308 / 0.37864, exact). STANDING RECOMMENDATION: do not re-index; DOCUMENT the units and support facts at the efv_score.py:1188-1196 seam and in p_bucket_given_fv's docstring; and treat the population gap as the binding defect, which xfv_odds_grade_basis 2.11(c) has already shown our cohort cannot refit above the `regular` bucket (pitcher good n = 11, star n = 2). The quality leg is SELECTED ON the denominator it divides by, so it is a bounded-below conditional read and may never be quoted as 'the board correlates X with quality'. EXPLOITATION, 7 arms, 0 promoted, on hit.full_pool_km (n=1783, floors 0.0295 E_refit / 0.0208 E_cond): multiplicative_pure -0.0892 (3.02x / 4.29x the floor), multiplicative_blend -0.0565 (1.92x / 2.72x) and multiplicative_blend_cal -0.0247 (0.84x / 1.19x) are RESOLVABLE LOSSES; hurdle_blend -0.0039, hurdle_blend_cal -0.0018, auxiliary_gamma_1.0 -0.0096 and auxiliary_gamma_1.0_cal -0.0108 are NULL. (3) MAE runs +0.0550 WAR above consensus, unfloored, and cannot arbitrate a board (honest_note). The era split reads +0.0542 on 2022-2023 against -0.0192 on cohorts to 2018.

HISTORY (2026-06 to 2026-08, retained so the retirement is legible rather than silent):
LEAN model (multi-season PEAK K-rate + final K-rate + bb_rel + age-vs-level + x_era_k + fastball), guarded blend. peak_k_rel flipped pitchers from trailing to BEATING consensus on OOS rank; bb_rel completed the K-BB edge. 2026-06-22 feature re-test added x_era_k = (-era_rel)*k_rel (run-prevention x missing-bats interaction): debuted-KM ridge 0.2739 -> 0.2823 (edge over consensus +0.063), full-pool 0.209 -> 0.215, blend +0.0074, sane calibration, robust 3/4 folds; era_rel alone fails (it is specifically the interaction). THE PLAN EXPECTED A GATE AND FOUND A WIRING DEFECT: the 2026-07-30 leak-free rebuild exists and the eFV model cannot see it. efv_model._observed_pos_map reads data/positions_played.json, the ORIGINAL career-to-date pre-debut census (2,756 players; measured coverage 33.5% of the matrix, 5.1% of debuted rows, 55.9% of bust rows, so the figures recorded in efv_model.py are intact and nothing about that artifact changed), while data/positions_played_seasons.json (3,827 players, league-wide, per-season, no debut filter, with the as_of rule in fielding_positions.season_visible_through) is not wired into the model at any point. The blocker was therefore never only a data job; it is now a consumer-repoint job as well, and it is a real defect that the model is gated against the worse of two artifacts it already has on disk. THE UNBLOCKING CRITERION IS THAT COVERAGE NO LONGER SEPARATES, AND IT STILL SEPARATES, by 13.5pp, in the opposite direction from before. A feature whose DEFINITION correlates with the label is the leak shape the flag exists for, and 13.5pp is a smaller lever than 50.8pp but a ridge can still learn it, so running a fit would have measured the residual leak and reported it as a feature. Scale if it is ever unblocked: on the as-of route 414 of 1,759 covered training rows change pos_prem (355 gain the premium, 59 lose it) against 122 of 642 on the old artifact. What the consumers are waiting on is now precisely identified as (a) the _observed_pos_map repoint and (b) either dropping the 87 unresolvable rows or accepting the 6.5pp residual, both of which are modelling decisions that owe their own gate.

models.notes: LANE-PROV-MAP, owner decision 2026-07-30: re-point the provisional grade map onto the board's map, with a gate. Pre-registration on disk BEFORE any code edit or candidate score: docs/efv-2026-07-30/PROVISIONAL_GRADE_MAP_GATE.md PART 1. VERDICT: NO SHIP. CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE, made first: efv_ungraded._grade was NEVER on realized_implied_fv (git log -S returns nothing); the module has always carried its own bespoke linear map, so the platform has THREE maps of predicted WAR, not two. The coherence complaint is nonetheless real and is now sized: prospx.buildEfvRankMap sorts 4,520 graded ACTIVE rows and 3,404 provisional rows together on the single xfv_grade field, and storage._top_end_points / _depth_points rank the farm pool on it, so a ten-FV map gap through the 1.5-3.5 predicted-WAR band is a silent demotion in two served orderings - the exact demotion the 2026-07-25 F2 repair retired when it set _PROV_RANK_PENALTY = 0. THREE OF SIX STOP CONDITIONS FIRE. (1) THE CAP. Under the incumbent affine map an FV constant is also a WAR constant; under outcome_implied_fv the two readings come apart. Pitcher KNEE 34 binds at 2.000 predicted WAR today and at 0.061 after a re-point, CEIL 38 at 2.889 and at 0.176: rows above the knee go 176 to 1,416 of 2,087 pitchers (8.4% to 67.9%), so keeping the FV constants converts a top-end bound into a near-universal compressor and piles 980 arms against a four-FV wall (V0 pitcher max 38.0, p90 37.9, p99 38.0). The WAR-space translation is EXACT (verified numerically, max |dFV| = 0.000000 on a 0.01-WAR grid) and preserves the cap's action identically, but its FV outputs breach the module's words: hitter max 49.5 above the CEIL 49 asymptote, and a cameo capped at 'org filler' would print 40.9 hit / 42.9 pit instead of 30. Neither branch is a no-op, so 'leave the cap alone' was the destructive option, not the conservative one. (2) THE DOCUMENTED CALIBRATION. The module's spec is 'MOST land 20-30', 'a true 45+ would have been graded', 'hitters median ~23 / 77% <= 30; pitchers median ~24 / 87% <= 30'. Pooled share <= 30 falls 0.923 to 0.641 (V0) / 0.491 (V1); rows >= 35 go 71 to 1,185 / 1,696; rows >= 45 go 1 to 32 / 62. Under V1 the median un-scouted org PITCHER is a 40.5 FV and 1,114 of 2,087 are 40 or better, up from zero. MECHANISM: 48.5% of the pool (1,650 of 3,404) has non-positive predicted WAR and outcome_implied_fv returns exactly 20.0 for all of it, so the re-point deletes the org-filler ladder the bespoke map exists to provide and leaves two spikes. That is the curve's own documented behaviour below its data floor applied to a population that is essentially entirely below it - and by that same documentation ('a grade under about 45 is a display re-spread, never present it as calibrated') the re-point buys COHERENCE and ZERO CALIBRATION here. (3) THE DIRECTION. data/xfv_thin_pbust_eval.json G1 measured this population's realized bust rate at provisional grade >= 35 as 0.881 hit / 0.940 pit, exceeding what the graded-population curve served by +0.169 CI95 [0.128,0.204] and +0.130 CI95 [0.094,0.150]. On exactly that cohort (71 served rows) V1 moves the mean grade 38.17 to 46.33 (hit) and 36.24 to 45.51 (pit), so p_bucket_given_fv reads them at 0.448 / 0.488 against measured 0.881 / 0.940 and the gap widens from +0.121/+0.130 to +0.433/+0.452. The grade would become ten FV more generous exactly where the only outcome evidence this population has says it is already too generous. PASSES: the row set is intact (3,404 of 3,404 graded under both branches), and within-side monotonicity in predicted WAR is EXACT - the 68-70 raw violations are all cameo-cap artifacts and 69 of them exist under the INCUMBENT map, so both maps are strictly increasing as documented. BLAST RADIUS if it had shipped: V1 moves 2,688 of 3,404 rows (95.3% of pitchers), mean dFV +5.44, mean |dFV| 7.15, max 13.7; 61 rows cross FV45 upward and 0 down (that line gates the client fv-45 colour band, the card-rarity shine tier, and storage.FV_POINTS, where the 40-to-45 step is 1.0 to 3.5 points); all 30 orgs' farm top-end+depth points change, league total 3,488 to 4,413 (+26.5%), provisional rows inside org top-25s 82 to 434; on the prospx joint board 4,393 of 4,520 GRADED rows move a median of 934 places while the top 100 is identical (0 in, 0 out). THE SEVEN ORPHANS split honestly: jacob_friend 35.1 to 44.8 (against the 43.5 he lost, so the re-point is right on that row) but mason_guerra 26.2 to 20.0 (he carried 37.5 on the flagship board and his -0.200 predicted WAR has one value under the new map). EPOCH/FINGERPRINT, confirmed not assumed: BOARD_RANK_BASIS_EPOCH would NOT need to move (overall_rank is built over `actives`, and a provisional player has points == [] so export_timeseries_json routes him to inactives before any other gate; _board_grade reads data/xfv.json only), but BOARD_BASIS_FINGERPRINT SHOULD name the provisional scale and does not - the prospx joint board is an ordering provisional grades enter, so a provisional-scale change is a board-ordering change the fingerprint cannot see. That gap exists today independent of this verdict and is registered as a follow-up rather than fixed, because changing the fingerprint suppresses the eFV-delta movement signal for a run. FOLLOW-UP SHAPE: any real fix needs an instrument with display granularity below FV 45 (re-anchoring the bespoke map's BASE and SLOPE to agree with outcome_implied_fv over 1.5-5 predicted WAR while keeping a monotone spread below), scored against realized outcomes rather than coherence. Read-only lane: no production module edited, no served number moved, data/xfv_ungraded.json untouched. Verdict recorded as 'deprecated', the enum's value for a measured no-ship.

models.notes:
CURRENT STATE (2026-09-24): served grade map (data/xfv_ungraded.json meta.grade_map) is hitters 27 + 3.8w, soft knee 43 / ceiling 49; pitchers 25 + 4.5w, soft knee 34 / ceiling 38. Since 2026-10-02 (PV-07) provisional rows sit in their own PROSPX section with no board rank, ordered by provisional_v2's chance of a first grade and show on farm rosters and their own detail pages. The dated history below records earlier maps (pitcher knee 38 / ceil 42, max 42) and the retired opt-in toggle (state.showProvisional); neither is served. A DEDICATED no-FV production ridge (NOT the flagship; the flagship is FV-anchored and ABSTAINS on ungraded players). Imputing a constant FV into the shipped model FAILS (FV weight dominant -> production-only predictions floor at the -2 WAR clamp) -> a re-fit no-FV model is the fix. SCOPE OF THE ACCURACY FIGURE (PROVISIONAL_V2 D5, 2026-10-01): the gate battery in data/xfv_ungraded_eval.json scores the served grade, pair-weighted, against realized first-6yr WAR on the source-GRADED labelled pool the ridge is fitted on: hitters 0.267 (n 1,032), pitchers 0.115 (n 895) (battery.by_side.*.rho_grade_weighted). That is WAR skill on graded prospects, not grading skill: the labelled pool sits about two rungs above the served population (population block), and the figure says nothing about the grade a source will first assign. The low-minors ~0.22 / all-levels ~0.31 hitter and 0.09 -> 0.24 pitcher figures this row used to quote came from the legacy protocol and do not reproduce on current code (legacy_2026_07_14.reproduced_on_current_code_and_corpus: hitters 0.112 low-minors / 0.281 all-levels, pitchers 0.101 / 0.150). HITTERS keep level_rank; PITCHERS DROP it (it hurt the low-minors read when measured). AGAINST FIRST SOURCE GRADES (registry row provisional_first_grade, data/provisional_track_eval.json leg served_backdated, spent): the served grade has no level skill (Spearman 0.017 CI95 [-0.191, 0.225], MAE 6.21 against 4.54 for a constant, n 97) but does order who is graded next (AUC 0.826 against a level-rank null of 0.615). GRADE MAP = conventional linear war->FV with an ORDER-PRESERVING SOFT CAP (compress above a knee toward a ceiling), NOT a hard cap. CAP TEST (2026-06-23, owner asked 'is 43 too low / do we need a hard cap'): for HITTERS the uncapped grade carries REAL forward-chained signal above 43 (realized 6yr WAR bins [43,48) mean 3.43, [48+) mean 6.10; Spearman 0.29 among >=40) so a hard cap at 43 DISCARDED signal -> soft knee 43 / ceil 49 lets genuine young-for-level breakouts grade mid-to-high-40s; for PITCHERS signal above 40 is NOISE (Spearman 0.077, flat bins; top uncapped = small-sample high-K complex-ball spikes) so knee 38 / ceil 42 compresses hard. Soft so order is preserved (matters now that grades fold into the rank). Distribution: hit median ~23 / 77% <=30 / max ~49; pit median ~24.5 / 87% <=30 / max 42. Reliability shrinkage keeps small DSL lines from spiking. Franklin Primera (CPX, 19) = #1 ungraded hitter breakout at ~45. Unblocked only by the Baseball America backfill: with two scored sources per-source precision is mathematically unidentified (three second moments against four unknowns), and BA is the third instrument. BA identifies the weights and is NOT a term in the baseline - adding it to SCORED_SOURCES collapses the common set 4,284 -> 295. THE HEADLINE IS NOT ABOUT DENOISING. The shipped head-to-head claim no longer clears its floor under EITHER estimator on today's data against the consensus as served: delta +0.03138 against E_cond 0.0327 (0.960x) and E_refit 0.0353 (0.889x), where the 2026-08-08 registration had 1.031x E_cond WIN / 0.963x E_refit NULL. Attribution: -0.00180 (64%) is FRAME DRIFT from this program's own BA backfill and identity repairs changing the common set, -0.00103 (36%) is denoising. The E_refit floor itself barely moved (0.0352 registered vs 0.0353 re-measured), so XFV_HEADTOHEAD_MDE95 is NOT stale; the DELTA moved. Same failure shape as the s7.5 retraction. VERDICTS: registered primary P1 = UNINFORMATIVE, because its per-board-year centering made the baseline WORSE (rho 0.30703 vs served 0.31889) and decision rule 1 refuses to call eFV's +0.04324 over a handicapped baseline a win. AMENDMENT 2 corrected the primary to S3 (same GLS weights, global intercept, like-for-like with the incumbent); S3 = COLLAPSES at +0.03035 against 0.0338 (0.898x) and 0.0365 (0.832x). The correction moves the verdict AGAINST eFV, which is why it is a correction and not spec-shopping. Mechanism for P1's failure is measured, not guessed: +0.00793 of the pooled statistic is cross-cohort ranking, and per-year centering deletes exactly that. WHAT IT EXONERATES. Denoising bought only +0.00103 rho, against C-A1's oracle ceiling of +0.0040 which was registered in advance as the reason to expect this - so eFV's lead is NOT an artifact of a badly built consensus. Control C1 (weights swapped) is the worst arm at -0.02199, and control C2 finds 0 of 200 random admissible reweightings inside the shipped WEIGHT_CLAMP alpha range beat the served consensus. consensus.py's construction survives this lane with its reputation improved. The precision estimates are directionally right (GLS > equal weight > swapped, monotone under both centerings); only the magnitude is negligible. CONFOUNDS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The served consensus is not a two-source object, so the baseline could have lost on inputs rather than method: 2,894 of 3,234 rows (89.5%) carry exactly two sources, and restricted to those rows every arm keeps its ordering. NOT VINTAGE-DISCIPLINED and labelled so in the artifact: precision is estimable only for board years 2023-2026 while MIN_LAG_YEARS=3 holds the scored window at 2014-2024, so the baseline is DEFINED using rows it also scores. Legitimate for a baseline definition, never quotable as out-of-sample, and it handicaps eFV rather than the baseline. First year this can be A/B'd vintage-clean is 2027. PRE-COMMITMENT SHIPPED. The collapse branch fired, but its 'ship it as a baseline improvement' remedy does NOT apply - there is no improvement to ship at +0.001 sub-floor, and shipping it would break C-A1's zero-weights-ship discipline. What shipped is the second half: the conviction headline was rewritten, and the panel prints the 3.3% gap-closure share the pre-commitment named. ZERO WEIGHTS SHIP, unchanged. Prior was registered at 0.50 and scored: the edge did not survive, but for a reason the prior did not contemplate - it died mostly on frame drift and on never having been more than 1.03x its floor, not on denoising. Producer tools/efv_denoised_baseline_lab.py, parity-gated: it refuses to score unless its reconstructed frame is bit-identical to efv_mde_lab._load_h2h / _h2h_pass on all three legs. models.notes: PROVISIONAL means MEASURED AND NOT ADOPTED. B1, the plan's highest-expected-value betting item. UNDERPOWERED: the calibration ledger is the only place model prob, market fair prob and a settled outcome share a row, and it holds 140 rows across just 20 GAMES on 2 slates. Market Brier 0.25718 vs model 0.27143 (delta +0.01424) but the game-clustered CI is [-0.00991, +0.03929] and INCLUDES ZERO, so the market's apparent edge is not resolvable at this n. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS MORE USEFUL THAN THE BRIER: the weight sweep is monotone to w=1.0, i.e. the optimum sits ON THE BOUNDARY, and w=1 sets the fair price equal to the market price so every edge is identically zero and NO BET CAN EVER BE PUBLISHED. An optimum there means the model contributes nothing on this sample, not that a good weight was found; a blend is only a product for w < 1. Direction is consistent with the honest backtest, where the model loses to always-take-the-home-team. CLOCK: revisit at 150+ distinct games in the ledger, which accrues only as slates are priced and settled. Do NOT fit a weight before then.

THE FRAME DECIDES THE ANSWER, and each of the three tilts a different way: all base years +0.0313 at 0.881x its floor (not resolvable), pre-debut only +0.0625 at 1.679x (would read 'beats consensus'), vintage-matched +0.0040 at 0.131x (dead tie). Production oos_grades path reproduces the ordering: +0.0292 / +0.0602 / +0.0014. THE PRE-DEBUT FRAME IS NOT SHIPPED AS THE HEADLINE EVEN THOUGH IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT CLEARS A FLOOR, because its margin is earned partly by an asymmetry that favours eFV rather than by better ordering: the strip removes the rows where the CONSENSUS is advantaged and keeps the rows where eFV is. The defect it fixes is real and the fix is kept (the receipts table and the archetype table have stripped post-debut reads since the 2026-07-15 audit; the pooled head-to-head basis never did), but the verdict is read off the symmetric frame. PARITY: the incumbent frame reproduces data/source_backtest.json bit-identically on all four raters at n=3,234 before the strip is applied. DIRECTION CONTROL: the consensus scores 0.4003 on the removed post-debut rows against 0.3012 on the retained ones, confirming the stated mechanism. The vintage-matched cell carries the SMALLEST floor of the three (0.0303 against 0.0355 and 0.0372) because one row per player removes the duplication that inflates variance under player resampling, so the tie is measured more precisely than either alternative and is not a power excuse. LIMIT: floors here are the refit estimator. E_cond's floor for this statistic class is the smaller of the two (0.0322 against 0.0345 as registered in docs/EFV_GATE_STANDARD.md section 7.6), so no verdict above can flip toward LESS resolvable under it, but E_cond was not re-derived on these frames and that is owed. 2026-09-25 (owner answers FP3-1, FP3-3): the headline moved from vm1 to the timing-pinned frame vm2 (built in a8f97cfd as a headline candidate). The E_refit floor 0.0303 is CARRIED from vm1 (measured on eFV v1, 2026-08-13) and labelled so; re-measuring it would refit V2 with the timing pin inside every draw. The in-run E_cond floor on vm2 is 0.0127. Per-source cells (eFV vs PROSPX consensus, MLB Pipeline, FanGraphs, Spearman and contributor AUC) are ONE Holm family, k 6, alpha 0.05 one-sided on |delta|/sd; a cell prints a verdict word only when it survives. First read: eFV beats FanGraphs on Spearman (+0.0412, Holm floor 0.0393) and on AUC (+0.0352, Holm floor 0.0237); the other four cells are intervals only.

models.notes: C-1, pre-registered at docs/efv-2026-08-13/DISPERSION_REPAIR_GATE.md, which copies its first three PASS conditions verbatim from the 2026-07-29 pre-registration (docs/efv-2026-07-29/CALIBRATION_FINDINGS.md item 2) rather than inventing them. THE CORRECTION WORKS: slope 0.649 to 1.008 hit and 0.562 to 0.935 pit, overall MAE -12.5% and -8.7%, rows pinned at the -2.0 floor 51 to 6 and 22 to 10, Spearman shift -0.0032 and -0.0099 against floors 0.0206 and 0.0212. Parity reproduced the registered uncorrected slopes (0.6491 vs 0.6540, 0.5624 vs 0.5868). Controls clean: the corrected slope is outside both the permuted-prediction band ([-2.881,0.565] hit) and the permutation null. ALL THREE ORIGINALLY PRE-REGISTERED CLAUSES PASS ON BOTH SIDES. The gate nonetheless returns NO_SHIP because of a FOURTH clause this lane added today, tail MAE not worse, which fails both sides (7.13 to 8.39 hit, 5.81 to 6.71 pit). That clause was justified by 'the tail is where the board order and the dollars live', and that justification DOES NOT TRANSFER: an affine increasing map leaves board order identical and served surplus prices off xfv_grade_quantile, a rank-quantile map, so the dollar effect is exactly zero. The underlying trade is intrinsic rather than a defect of the family: a slope-1 map minimises squared error overall and necessarily pulls extremes toward the middle, so no affine correction improves level and tail together, and the gate's own stop clause forbids fitting a second family in search of a pass. REFERRED TO THE OWNER with both halves stated. LIMITS: the pitcher slope CI is wide [0.0677,1.1341]; folds are the registered 2016-2020 set, so a ship would re-fit coefficients on the production frame. SHIP BLOCKED 2026-08-13, found while implementing the owner's ship decision. The gate measured a property of xfv_war in isolation, but production does not serve it in isolation: xfv_war is the input to the board grade (xfv_grade = vf.outcome_implied_fv(xfv_war), efv_score.py:1473, monotone) AND the model leg of the blend (rank_war = (1-lam)*cons_war + lam*xfv_war, :1923). Applying at source moves every displayed grade and silently re-weights the blend to lam*b_c against 1-lam, a ~37% de facto lambda reduction at b_c ~0.63, which re-opens the BANNED blend-lambda lane by side effect. Applying only to the exported xfv_war_6yr leaves the grade derived from the uncorrected value and publishes a WAR and a grade that disagree. Doing both coherently is a GRADE-BASIS EPOCH (epoch bump, fingerprint term, prospx_current re-capture, golden restamp, every margin re-read), far larger than this gate scoped. This also CORRECTS the claim made earlier in the gate doc and to the owner that board order and dollars provably cannot move: true of the measured statistic, false of the field the correction must touch. LAMBDA RE-GATE QUANTIFIED 2026-08-13 (docs/efv-2026-08-13/SERVE_CHAIN_VERIFICATION.md). Routing the correction through the blend gives an equivalent pure lambda of lam*b_c/((1-lam)+lam*b_c): hitters 0.70 -> 0.5917, which lands beside the 0.60 the TOST battery already ruled out as a difference and is acceptable; PITCHERS 0.57 -> 0.3583 against a _BLEND_LAMBDA_CLAMP floor of 0.35, i.e. 0.008 above the model's own admissible minimum and far outside anything tested (TOST covered 0.65/0.60/0.51). Pitcher b_c is also the least stable quantity here, 0.308 to 0.651 across folds, matching its wide slope CI. So the full grade-basis epoch CANNOT ship on the pitcher side as specified: it would spend the calibration fix as an unmeasured lambda cut to the clamp floor. Remaining options are the narrow path (correct grade and exported WAR, leave the blend leg uncorrected, which touches no lambda and moves no dollars), a hitter-only epoch, or a separately gated pitcher lambda decision on its own evidence. OWNER DECISION 2026-08-13: THE NARROW PATH, superseding the earlier full-epoch choice which was made before the lambda number existed. Correct the GRADE and the EXPORTED WAR; leave the BLEND leg (rank_war) reading the uncorrected value. Lambda untouched, rank_war and therefore every quantile position unchanged so dollars provably do not move, board order provably identical since grade and board_sort_key are both strictly increasing in xfv_war. Displayed grade VALUES move, so it is still an epoch. Shipping session: re-fit a_c/b_c on the production frame (these are the registered 2016-2020 folds), apply at efv_score.py:1473 and the xfv_war_6yr emissions only and NOT at :1923, bump the epoch with a fingerprint term naming the correction, re-capture prospx_current inside vf.valuation_set, restamp golden, pin board order unchanged as a regression test since it is now provable, verify the surplus diff is zero rows rather than inheriting that claim, and disclose the tail cost. Accepted cost: grade and blend read two versions of one quantity, which must be written where a reader finds it. BASIS STAMP 2026-08-19: the correction was reverted to identity on the owner's decision (C-7, 2026-08-14) and the retired coefficients must never be applied.

THE METHODOLOGICAL FINDING, pre-registered before measuring: the same comparison on the OUTCOME-selected top decile favours the uncorrected arm RESOLVABLY on both sides (+1.1890 [0.832,1.526] hit, +0.5340 [0.377,0.683] pit). models.notes:
=== 2026-09-04c, THE PENALTY DECISION SHIPPED ===
The owner's rule was 'pitchers and not hitters if that is what the outcome evidence supports, and remove it if it is not proven'. Tested as the rule rather than as a feature: full pool, grade/age/exposure partialled out, bootstrap intervals, and a penalty keeps its place only if the interval excludes zero on the NEGATIVE side.
  PITCHERS n=1,220 rho -0.1664 CI95 [-0.2228, -0.1087] -> SUPPORTED
  HITTERS  n=1,127 rho +0.0651 CI95 [+0.0021, +0.1282] -> CONTRAINDICATED (above zero)
SHIPPED efv_score.INJURY_PENALTY_SIDES = {'pit'}. Removes the haircut from 225 served hitters (median x0.738, harshest x0.53) and leaves 360 pitchers untouched. Grade effect on the 225: 74 up, 150 flat, 1 down, mean +0.31 FV, max +4.6. The 150 flat sit at the FV20 floor where outcome_implied_fv is constant below 0 WAR; the 1 down (cameron_nelson) flips grade_basis provisional_capped -> outcome_pooled as model WAR crosses zero, which is the known floor-routing discontinuity, not a new defect. BOARD_BASIS_FINGERPRINT gained an injsides= term in the same commit; rides BOARD_RANK_BASIS_EPOCH 2026-09-04. Glossary copy corrected: it said the penalty applied to all live prospects AND still claimed post-TJ status was taxed, which the 2026-07-15 directive had already retired.
NOT CHANGED ON PURPOSE: the IL-type severity dispatch and the trailing days/stints deepening modifiers. Measurable only on the 144 pitchers the gate taxes, every interval spans zero, which at that width is LOW POWER rather than evidence of absence. Removing them would be acting on absence of evidence. Re-read when the cohort grows.

=== 2026-09-04, SECOND PASS. The archive was repaired, the population was corrected, and the lane is a NULL as a driver. Supersedes the first-pass reading below. ===
ARCHIVE FIXED, NOT WORKED AROUND. The first pass was blocked by injury history starting in 2019. That was OUR window, not the endpoint's: stats.TRANSACTIONS_LOOKBACK_SEASONS was 7. Probed with an explicit start_year the API returns IL events back to 2014 (Buxton) and 2016 (Nola). tools/backfill_player_transactions.py widened it with a superset guard and recovered 16,678 pre-2019 events across 1,684 of 2,260 players; the constant is now 16. Pre-decision coverage went 33.8 percent to 49.3 hit / 46.0 pit by row, and the observable cohort to 1,127 hit / 1,220 pit on the full pool. Archive reliability is now MEASURED, not assumed: the IL rate per ACTIVE player-year plateaus near 27 percent from 2017 and is depressed before it (2013 6.4, 2015 16.8, 2017 21.9), so observability is a window-coverage share against a 2017 floor rather than a cutoff on the decision year.
THE EXPOSURE CONFOUND IS THE FINDING. A player cannot be placed on an IL unless he is rostered, so 'no IL record' conflates healthy with never-exposed. On the full pool 576 of 1,127 observable hitters have NO record and they bust 83.7 percent against 68.6 percent for those with one, i.e. read raw the data says injuries are GOOD. The pool choice flips the sign on its own: hitter il_stints is -0.084 on debuted rows and +0.014 on the full pool. Debuted-only conditions on the outcome injuries most often prevent and must not be the population for this question.
EXPOSURE-CONTROLLED, PARTIALLING OUT THE GRADE AND ROSTERED-TIME PROXIES, THE ANSWER IS SIDE-ASYMMETRIC. HITTERS: every burden feature turns POSITIVE (il_days +0.165, il_max_stint_days +0.173, il_60day +0.203, il_days_ge_180 +0.193), so among hitters of equal grade, age and rostered time the ones who missed time did BETTER. PITCHERS: the control makes it worse, not better (debuted pool il_days -0.071 to -0.119, il_stints_ge_2 -0.093 to -0.112), and il_open_at_decision on the full pool goes -0.026 to -0.166.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHIPPED PENALTY (efv_score._injury_factor, a multiplicative haircut gated on il_on): the outcome evidence SUPPORTS it for pitchers and does NOT support it for hitters, where the controlled sign points the other way. It is currently applied to both sides identically. This is descriptive evidence on a live-board rule, so it is an owner decision and not an automatic change; the narrow version is to make the haircut pitcher-only or much weaker for hitters.
AS A DRIVER: NOTHING SHIPS, in any of the four side-by-pool cells. The stacked out-of-fold health submodel over stints, days, longest stint, 60-day and full-season counts is NEGATIVE everywhere (-0.003 to -0.057) and never clears its floor. The first pass's most promising cell, pitcher il_days_ge_90 at +0.0172, COLLAPSED to +0.0037 on the repaired cohort: it was a small-sample artifact, which is what the repair was for. Best surviving cell is hitter il_days_ge_30 at +0.0133 against a 0.0149 floor, Holm 0.44.
TOMMY JOHN CANNOT BE ANSWERED ON THE PROSPECT WINDOW and no archive fix changes it: minor-league placements name the injury 3.2 percent of the time (319 of 10,039) against 54.5 percent in the majors, so the prospect-window TJ cell is n=1. Answering it needs the MLB side, which is a different question from the one this driver asks.
ONE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE REPORTING: the first submodel build scored -0.174 with p 0.000 on hitters. That was mine, not the data's. The raw out-of-fold score is a WAR-scale prediction whose LEVEL drifts by fold (per-fold means 4.08, 5.03, 4.36, 3.81, 4.06, 3.63) and whose first fold has no prior data at all, so it was encoding cohort year. Standardised within decision year it reads -0.003, a clean null.

=== first pass, 2026-09-04, superseded above ===
Owner ask 2026-09-04. THE DESCRIPTIVE SIGNAL IS REAL AND CONSISTENT. Hitters, observable cohort 444: no IL placement at all gives mean 4.08 WAR vs 2.62, star 16.1 vs 9.6 percent, bust 44.8 vs 52.6; four or more stints gives mean 1.42 vs 3.34 and star 5.9 vs 12.7. Pitchers, cohort 559: no placement gives mean 2.15 vs 1.40 and star 5.9 vs 2.9 percent; two or more stints cuts the star rate to 1.3 from 5.4; il_days rho -0.080 and il_max_stint_days -0.083. So cumulative IL burden as a prospect really does track worse outcomes and durability tracks better ones. GATED, NOTHING SURVIVES HOLM: the best cell is pitcher il_days_ge_90 at +0.01722, which CLEARS its 0.01531 floor with permutation p 0.005 but lands at Holm 0.10 in a family of 20. That is the closest any 2026-09-04 candidate came to shipping.
THE INCUMBENT PENALTY LOOKS BACKWARDS. il_open_at_decision, which is the signal the current IL haircut uses, associates with BETTER outcomes in this cohort on both sides: hitters mean 3.80 vs 3.10 and star 17.5 vs 11.4 percent, pitchers star 7.7 vs 3.9. n is 57 and 52 and the cohort is selected, so this is not a verdict, but it is evidence that penalising current IL status is at best unsupported. Do not remove the haircut on this alone; do not defend it on outcomes either.
COVERAGE IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and it is a DATA problem not a modelling one. il_history is not a history (1,415 of 1,662 placements are 2026, first populated 2026-06-06). The real source is player_transactions: 27,255 IL events on 4,887 players with placements AND activations, so days are computable, but it starts in 2019. Pre-decision coverage is therefore 0 percent for debut years 2016-2018 and 39 to 79 percent for 2020-2024, leaving 52.5 percent of hitter and 56.9 percent of pitcher rows observable and only 311 and 455 scored rows. A full-pool feature would encode DEBUT ERA rather than health. What would change the verdict: a longer injury archive, not a better model.

models.champion: the LEXICOGRAPHIC objective, accuracy first: a market may set a threshold only when its accuracy leg is non-inferior to the market open on the same games (paired per-game Brier lb95 >= -0.002, floor 100 same-games comparisons) AND its ROI leg clears lb95 > 0 at n >= 100 inside ONE (market, rule) cell. A market that fails the accuracy leg has its ROI leg REPORTED and NOT CONSULTED. CLV is one key carrying the reason it does not exist, never a null column
models.baseline: The de-vigged market open on the same games, with the same-games base rate and, on the moneyline, literature Elo
models.metric: Accuracy: paired Brier vs the open, lb95 >= -0.002, 100+ games; ROI: flat-stake lb95 > 0, 100+ rows
models.notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 AND EVERY MARKET FAILS THE ACCURACY LEG, so the ROI leg never had to be consulted. Vintage eval window from 2026-08-01, 487 graded games, 22 slates with an open capture; every tier scored on the same-games window for its market. Paired per-game Brier, model minus market open (positive means the model is better): moneyline n=254, model 0.24576 vs open 0.23467, delta -0.011093 at t -1.929, lb95 -0.020556. Runline n=247, model 0.23649 vs open 0.23163, delta -0.004859 at t -0.636, lb95 -0.017432. Total n=250 (6 pushes dropped), model 0.27530 vs open 0.25128, delta -0.024015 at t -2.431, lb95 -0.040268. The bar is -0.002 and all three miss it. Log loss same pairs: -0.027083, -0.010600, -0.084821. Against the same-games base-rate constant instead of the open: moneyline +0.003681 (t 1.664, lb95 +0.000042), runline +0.013309 (t 1.170), total -0.025312 (t -2.537). THE TOTAL IS WORSE THAN ITS OWN BASE RATE at two and a half standard errors, which is the section 11a Poisson underdispersion showing up in a market rather than in a variance ratio; the moneyline is the only market that beats a constant, and it does so by less than it loses to the open. ROI leg, per_market_cap era, one row per (market, rule) cell: moneyline::board_all n=43 ROI -0.30925 lb95 -0.56745; moneyline::longshot n=4 ROI -0.22500 lb95 -1.32907; moneyline::potd_band n=9 ROI +0.08686 lb95 -0.47750; runline::board_all n=71 ROI -0.01306 lb95 -0.18604; runline::potd_band n=6 ROI -0.47935 lb95 -0.97385; total::board_all n=100 ROI -0.12844 lb95 -0.28706. One cell of six meets the 100-row floor and none clears. Quarter-Kelly realized log growth per bet, same cells: -0.009373, +0.001668, +0.001876, -0.003200, -0.025869, -0.008189. The order mattered: had ROI been read first, moneyline::potd_band at +8.7% over nine bets is exactly the row a rule reads as encouraging. CLV IS UNAVAILABLE AND SAYS SO IN ONE KEY (roi.clv_unavailable): 'close job never installed; 0 settled ledger rows carry a close price', measured over 22 cached odds snapshots all of kind open, zero of kind close, and 0 of 255 ledger rows carrying a close price under any name. VERIFICATION: the second snapshot walker (_market_open_by_market) reproduces the section 6 ladder's own same_games block to the digit on the moneyline (n 254, open 0.23467, model 0.24576, constant 0.24944, Elo 0.24505), so it is the same walker widened to three markets and the published ladder is untouched.

SAME SECTION, SECOND LANE (B-ML-FIT), recorded here because it shares the artifact and the doc section and has no row of its own: the vintage OLS fit is wrong-signed on its most important term and the obvious repair was gated and LOST. On the 305-game vintage fit half b1 (the scoring team's OWN offense) is -0.037205 at r2 = 0.003, and diff_shrink comes back at 1.28, expanding what a shrink parameter exists to contract. A sign-constrained ridge shrunk toward LITERATURE_COEFFS (b1 > 0, b2 < 0, b3 > 0, penalty chosen on the fit half by moneyline log loss on an inner 0.75 date split, solved exactly over the eight faces of the constrained orthant) was gated at split quantiles 0.6/0.7/0.8 on non-inferiority (paired Brier lb95 >= -0.001), superiority over the literature Elo tier (t >= 1.645) and log loss not worse. Grid: q=0.6 delta -0.000221 lb95 -0.000774, q=0.7 delta -0.000203 lb95 -0.000553, q=0.8 delta +0.000213 lb95 -0.000611; one split of three passes, so the verdict is INDETERMINATE and betting_model.SERVE_RIDGE_FIT stays False. On the SERVED window (fit 305 / eval 487) the ridge at penalty 0.3 repairs every symptom (b1 -0.037205 to +0.041543, b3 0.594771 to 3.157603, diff_shrink 1.28 to 1.08, home adjustment -0.0443 to +0.0063) and grades WORSE: Brier 0.24460 to 0.24522, delta -0.000617 at t -0.812, lb95 -0.001868. The finding is about the FEATURE, not the solver: at the constrained optimum the own-offense term is pinned to EXACTLY zero at all three gate splits, so on vintage features it is not paying for itself. Check 2 is a bar on the model class rather than on the challenger, and the artifact persists elo.ols_vs_elo beside elo.ridge_vs_elo so that cannot be misread (the incumbent misses the Elo bar itself at q=0.6, t 1.625, and lands exactly on it at q=0.7, t 1.645). THIRD LANE: growing the vintage fit window was also measured and also lost. fit_window_probe holds the eval window and varies only the fit (the two halves are complements, so the shipped configurations are not paired and cannot be compared directly): anchored 305 games vs grown, paired Brier, positive means grown is better, q=0.6 -0.002789 (t -2.107, lb95 -0.004967), q=0.7 -0.000133 (t -0.162, lb95 -0.001482), q=0.8 +0.001750 (t +0.867, lb95 -0.001570). ALL THREE splits miss the -0.001 bar, the 0.8 split included: its point estimate favours growth but 165 eval games do not buy an interval that clears the bar. So VINTAGE_FIT_WINDOW_GROWS stays False; the grown fit is worse while looking healthier (its b3 at q=0.6 is 2.83 against the anchored 0.59, much nearer the literature 3.20, and it still grades 0.00279 of Brier worse on the same 323 games). Coefficient plausibility and out-of-sample accuracy point in opposite directions on this sample, twice. NOTHING IN THIS LANE CHANGED A SERVED NUMBER: three measurements, three flags left where they were.

models.notes: A-CLAIM-11, shipped 2026-09-06. INSTRUMENT PROOF, run 2026-09-06 at B=2000, seed 20260807, 739 s, ALL CONTROLS PASS. A0 parity: the numpy AUC reproduces source_backtest._auc (the function efv_model._auc_breakdown calls) to abs diff exactly 0.0 on all four cells, so the leg measures the served statistic and not a lookalike. A0b: the driver pool carries one row per player_key (839 hit / 981 pit, zero repeats), so the i.i.d. row bootstrap is admissible here and the 1.519x clustered narrowing of section 7.6 is a property of the head-to-head frame, not this one. A3 label permutation, K=2000: mean AUC 0.500243 hit (z +0.50) and 0.499691 pit (z -0.62), empirical sd 1.0032x / 0.9907x the analytic Hanley-McNeil null SE, so the null is centred AND as wide as theory. Both A3 bars are two-sided by section 7.4. A3's bar was re-sized ONCE before any arm ran and the reason is on the record: the first specification (|mean-0.5| < 2 SEM at K=200) failed on the hitter side at z=2.47, re-measurement at K=4000 on three seeds put the hitter at |z| 0.44/1.08/0.25 and the pitcher at 1.52/1.02/0.80, so the null was centred and a 2-SEM bar simply false-fails 4.6 percent of the time per side by construction. ZERO-INFORMATION TWIN: all three noise arms land inside their own floor on all four statistics both sides (hit AUC points +0.00420/+0.00150/+0.00208 against the 0.0091 floor; pit +0.00157/-0.00011/-0.00068 against 0.0068), and a row-permuted real column (fv_trend) lands at AUC +0.00352 hit (0.39x) / -0.00096 pit (0.14x) and rho 0.24x / 0.12x, verdict NULL on both. THE RULE FIRED ON THE FIRST REAL COLUMN IT SAW: unpermuted fv_trend on the pitcher side reads contributor AUC +0.00741 at 1.09x its floor while pooled rho is +0.00160 at 0.13x, which is NULL_AUC_ONLY under the rule and would have been a headline without it. That is an illustration and NOT an adjudication of fv_trend (it was carrying the twin, it did not run the full battery, and the D-1 ledger's +0.01028 for the same key is on the pre-epoch labels). Star AUC is a sensitivity because the pitcher star cell is 51 positives at 5.7 percent prevalence on this frame and 46 positives against an E_cond floor of 0.0397 in the registered data/xfv_auc_floor_eval.json cell: a leg that cannot resolve its own null cannot adjudicate anyone's arm. Population is the debuted pool only, so the full-pool debut/no-debut cell the section 3 carve-out rules INADMISSIBLE is unreachable from this lab by construction. The AUC legs are UNWEIGHTED while the rho legs are pair-weighted (control C-a), inherited from the served chain and reported rather than quietly fixed. NO CLAIM OF POWER IS MADE: this lane measured a floor and showed the instrument returns nulls on nulls; it adjudicated no driver arm and moved no served number. OPEN: data/xfv_driver_floors.json still predates the leg, so freekeys_mode reads no AUC floor and reports 'no floor derived' for that leg until `python tools/efv_driver_lab.py floor 2000` is re-run; that is coded to fail safe rather than borrow a constant. There is no E_cond leg in this lab, so a claim taken from it must name E_refit. Measured contributor-AUC floors hit 0.0091 / pit 0.0068. data/xfv_driver_floors.json is regenerating to carry these floors; until it does, the gate returns NOT_ADJUDICATED_NO_AUC_FLOOR for every arm, which is intended.]
