models.summary: Shipped 2026-09-06 as a consistency repair, not an accuracy claim: one distribution per market; on strikeouts the binomial beats Poisson by 0.001045 Brier. No prop odds captured.
models.surface: /betting/ props tab fair-line table, every row priced through this distribution; the book-compared block is inert
models.predicts: The count distribution for one player prop (strikeouts, hits, total bases, home runs) and its Over, Under and push probabilities
models.champion: one distribution declared per market in betting_export.PROPS_DISTRIBUTIONS, shared by the fair-line table and the value block: BINOMIAL over expected plate appearances for 1+ hits and 1+ home runs and over expected batters faced for strikeouts and hits allowed, because those counts are sums of per-trial indicators with support capped at the trial count; POISSON for total bases and earned runs, because both are compound sums with no per-trial cap (a plate appearance yields 0 to 4 bases) and the extra-base mix a compound distribution needs is not carried on the row. A fractional expected trial count is priced as a mixture of the two adjacent integer trial counts, which preserves the mean at exactly lambda and is continuous in expected PA; rounding instead would put a 1.35 point step in the middle of a lineup card (at lambda 1.2, Binomial(4, 0.30) reads 0.75990 for 1+ against Binomial(5, 0.24)'s 0.74645).
models.baseline: The blanket Poisson that priced the value block before 2026-09-06, at the same mean and line
models.metric: Paired Brier on the line vs alternative distributions at the same mean, game-clustered; binomial beats Poisson by 0.001045 on strikeouts
models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-09-06 AS A CONSISTENCY REPAIR, NOT AN ACCURACY CLAIM. The defect: props_fair_lines priced 1+ hits and 1+ home runs as a per-PA Bernoulli complement (1 - (1 - p) ** exp_pa) while props_value_bets priced the SAME two markets as a Poisson through _props_side_probabilities, so one page carried two probabilities for one bet. Measured on a slot-1 hitter (exp_pa 4.65, lambda 1.60, per-PA rate 0.34409) at the 0.5 line: Bernoulli 0.85929, Poisson 0.79810, gap 0.06118; the single binomial path reads 0.85630. At the 1.5 line the two surfaces had no shared answer at all because the fair-line path only ever priced 0.5 (Poisson 0.47507 against the binomial's 0.51338). On a whole 2.0 line the push mass itself was wrong, 0.25843 Poisson against 0.32413 binomial, and _priced_side scales published EV by (1 - p_push). Population size of the change on the real projection lines in data/fantasy.json: across 471 hitters at DEFAULT_PA 4.20, binomial minus Poisson is a median +0.04179 at the 0.5 line (range +0.02922 to +0.05293, always positive because the binomial puts less mass on a hitless game) and a median -0.00658 at the 1.5 line (range -0.01115 to +0.00491, the sign flipping with whether lambda sits above or below the line); across 203 projected starters at a 5.2 inning start, strikeouts move a median +0.00396 (range -0.00834 to +0.01896), smaller because 22 batters faced is close enough to unbounded that the two nearly agree. The batters-faced trial count is measured, not assumed: bf is present on 272 of 272 projected pitchers at a median 4.30 batters per inning. The Poisson was also assigning 0.00604 of its mass to more than 5 hits in 4.65 plate appearances, an outcome with no sample space. NO SERVED NUMBER MOVED because no props row is served. Every fair-line row and every value row now carries model_id and pmf, and a market that declares a binomial but is handed no trial count prices Poisson and states that in pmf_basis rather than falling back silently. Regression fence: test_betting_props_pmf.py, 18 tests, all passing standalone on 2026-09-06 (python test_betting_props_pmf.py); the existing 19 in test_betting_props.py also pass unchanged. [2026-09-06: the distribution choice is now measured rather than argued. The served choice survives on the line leg; the REASON shipped beside it was backwards on dispersion and has been replaced. See betting_props_k_dark.] THE TRIAL COUNT MOVED 2026-09-17 (plan repair 8, audit L17-F3, pre-registered as B-PA-DIST): expected plate appearances by lineup slot were a hand rule, 4.65 at the leadoff spot falling a flat 0.10 a slot, which handed nine starters 38.25 plate appearances out of the 37.63 a team-game carries, so every hitter Over on the board was priced a little high. It is now a COUNT off the cached play-by-play corpus (tools/props_slot_pa_lab.py, artifact data/betting_props_slot_pa_eval.json, flag betting_export.SERVE_SLOT_PA_MEASURED), fitted on 2022-2024 (131,202 starter-games) and held out once on 2025 (43,740), SPLIT HOME FROM AWAY because the home club does not bat in the ninth when it leads: leadoff 4.5785 away against 4.3873 at home, nine hole 3.5652 against 3.3711, a 0.16 to 0.20 PA gap at every slot. Acceptance, both legs pre-registered: hold-out PA MAE 0.54793 against the hand rule's 0.57540 pooled and 0.51945 against 0.57749 over the slots 1 to 5 the board actually prices, paired t clustered by team-game 12.65 and 28.63, and the split table also beats the pooled one (t 7.98); each side's nine slots sum under that side's own PA per team-game (away 37.0718 of 38.4586, home 35.4739 of 36.8061). WHERE IT LOSES, on the record: hold-out MAE is worse than the hand rule at slot 7 (0.55801 against 0.51918) and slot 8 (0.63476 against 0.56866), neither of them priced. Served move on the 2026-09-17 board, 39 hitter rows and 117 sides, every one down: total bases P(over) -0.0177 mean and -0.0335 worst, 1+ hits -0.0124, 1+ home runs -0.0045. No moneyline, runline or total price is touched, so MODEL_VERSION does not bump, and props value bets stay unarmed. Not conditioned on, from B-PA-DIST's brief and said plainly: run environment and extra innings, neither knowable when a row is priced. The fallback for an unreadable slot moved 4.20 to 4.2875, the mean of the slots this table prices, and a row that reaches it says so in expected_pa_basis.

models.summary: Measured: the sort key inverts on 3.3% of hitter and 3.9% of pitcher pairs; the outcome-curve map is exactly monotone, the provisional map inverts on 25.4% and 48.8%.

models.notes: 2026-09-06 (A-CLAIM-7). THE ORDER IS FINE: the sort key inverts against the evaluated object on 3.3% of untied hitter pairs and 3.9% of pitcher pairs, rho 0.9876 and 0.9855, reproducing the figures the 2026-09-05 plan projected. THE FLAGSHIP MAP IS EXACTLY MONOTONE: zero inversions over ~880,000 untied pairs across both sides, so efv_score.py's monotonicity docstring is true where it applies. THE PROVISIONAL MAP IS NOT: served to 1,091 hitters (51% of the side) and 1,386 pitchers (58%), it inverts against the model's own predicted WAR on 25.4% and 48.8% of untied pairs, and half is what independence looks like. Every provisional row carries consensus FV exactly 35.0, so this basis IS the no-published-opinion population A-CLAIM-12 counts, reached from the other direction. Routing (pairs graded through different maps) accounts for 57.9% of all hitter grade discordance and 37.8% of pitcher. NOT NECESSARILY A DEFECT: a player with no professional track record is graded off a prior rather than off a ridge prediction nobody should trust yet. It had never been measured, and it bounds what the head-to-head result covers.

models.notes: 2026-09-06 (M-ENG-1). Brier 0.1559 against a 0.2498 base rate, skill 0.377, expected calibration error 0.0066, fit on 1,448,965 plays. MLB's own live number scores 0.1577 on the same plays, so this team-blind model is very slightly ahead; that is not a claim to have beaten MLB at win probability, it settles that insisting on a team-blind valuation costs nothing measurable. THREE DESIGNS WERE TRIED AND THE FIRST TWO ARE ON THE RECORD BECAUSE THEY LOOKED FINE. (1) Raw cell means: advancing a runner from first to second LOWERED the batting team's win expectancy in 42.6% of cells, pure estimation noise at 318 observations per cell. (2) A smooth model with a separate bottom-half term: monotone in the base state but discontinuous across the half-inning boundary, pricing 19.2% of steal attempts so that being caught stealing HELPED. (3) The batting-team frame plus a measured boundary table: zero violations on the population that is actually priced. Two further defects fixed en route, both silent: base occupancy read with astype(bool) on a runner-id column made every base look occupied (bool(NaN) is True), and per-cell masking dropped a different six-figure run-expectancy cell on every build. RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-10 after audit finding F07-02: the win model was fitted and queried on a POST-play score against a PRE-play base-out state, so every decision on this surface was priced on leaked values. Refit on the honest state; the gate battery was re-run rather than assumed and its verdict is unchanged (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, split-half 0.1098 inside its null band). The league running-game net flipped sign (+1.79 to -0.75 wins) and the served Brier claim reversed (the MLB feed now leads 0.157516 to 0.157678).

models.notes: 2026-09-06. 13,971 priced attempts over 2018-2026. THE FINDING: the league steals second at a 75.00% success rate against a swing-weighted break-even of 75.03%, so eight seasons of decision value sum to -0.19 wins. Managers collectively run the stolen base at almost exactly the point of indifference. Stealing third is worth +4.31 wins (76.1% against 72.8%); stealing home is worth -2.33 (25.8% against 55.8%). TWO-OUT ATTEMPTS ARE EXCLUDED, 9,328 of them, about 40% [CORRECTED 2026-09-11, audit F02-01: 11,783 of 26,139, about 45%. The caught stealings that END a plate appearance live only on the play's own result and were never read]: with two down a caught stealing ends the inning, so the alternative is priced by a different estimator from the hold, and that mismatch valued up to 19.2% of attempts so that being caught stealing HELPED. AN OPEN QUESTION WAS CLOSED BY THE SAME EXCLUSION: failed attempts appeared to carry 1.5 times the win-probability swing of successful ones, which invited a reading about defences bearing down; it was mechanical, and with the inning-ending attempts removed the ratio is 1.00. PROVISIONAL AND NOT ATTRIBUTED: no number here is assigned to a manager, because the manager entity and the gate battery (split-half stability, placebo, persistence, captured share) have not been built. [2026-09-06, gate result: the family is a bounded NULL. Season-controlled split-half r 0.0691 inside [-0.1504, 0.1243], ICC 0.00538, implied true between-agent spread 0.0130 wins per team-season. No decision value may be attributed to an agent from this family, and the manager entity is NOT worth fetching for it.] RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-10 after audit finding F07-02: the win model was fitted and queried on a POST-play score against a PRE-play base-out state, so every decision on this surface was priced on leaked values. Refit on the honest state; the gate battery was re-run rather than assumed and its verdict is unchanged (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, split-half 0.1098 inside its null band). The league running-game net flipped sign (+1.79 to -0.75 wins) and the served Brier claim reversed (the MLB feed now leads 0.157516 to 0.157678). CENSUS REPAIRED 2026-09-11 (audit F02-01): management.py read the corpus events table alone, and a steal that ends a plate appearance is not a playEvent but the play's own result, so 2,475 attempts that exist only there, such as a caught stealing for the third out, were neither priced nor counted while the artifact said the excluded attempts were counted. Both tables are read now and the artifact's attempt_census holds priced plus excluded equal to the corpus count (13,973 + 12,166 = 26,139). The few recovered attempts below two out joined the priced pool, so stealing third now reads +5.99 wins on 1,934 attempts. The gate was re-run: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, split-half 0.1085 inside [-0.1501, 0.1272].

THE ROUTE SPLIT WAS 342-TO-12 WRONG BEFORE IT WAS CHECKED: StatsAPI's notes field is EMPTY on 333 of 354 recipients and several of the 21 that carry one say things like 'No cap logo on plaque', so defaulting an empty note to the writers reported twelve committee inductees when the committees have elected more players than the writers. FOUR PARSER DEFECTS, each found against the live page: a dotted player id (sabatc.01), a non-breaking space inside every marked name, an enshrinement marker that is a perfect outcome leak and is now named bref_hof_marker_as_of_scrape so nobody uses it as a feature, and a latin-1 double-decode that silently broke the join for every accented player. A CENSORED PLAYER NEVER CARRIES A ZERO, asserted by assert_no_censored_zero over the real frame rather than by prose: a zero there says the voters decided no about somebody they have not finished deciding on, it biases every recent cohort toward zero, it does it hardest to the best candidates, and it is silent. A player who NEVER APPEARED on a ballot is also censored, not zero, because the screening committee's decision not to list him is a different event from the writers voting him down and this panel cannot tell them apart. THE ONE ARBITRARY CONSTANT is COMMITTEE_HORIZON_YEARS, default 25: the era committees never formally close and have elected players fifty years after retirement, so on a strict reading no non-inductee is ever a resolved zero and the negative class is empty. The horizon is marked an assumption where it is defined and label_sensitivity() publishes what 15, 20, 30 and 40 would do instead.

models.notes: 2026-09-06 (M-MWAR-4). THE FAMILY IS A NULL AND THE NULL IS BOUNDED. Season-controlled split-half r = 0.0691 inside a permutation band of [-0.1504, 0.1243]; one-way ICC 0.00538; implied true between-agent spread 0.0130 wins per team-season. The detection floor says the battery would have seen a per-attempt effect of 0.0005 at 80 percent power, so this is a ceiling rather than an absence. A FALSE PASS WAS CAUGHT ON THE WAY. A first reading reported that summed decision value cleared its null; two things were wrong at once. The null reassigned attempt counts, which destroys the structure under test, and the series was RAW decision value, which correlates at +0.7789 across split halves while season alone explains 0.7961 of its variance and team identity explains 0.0223. A prior design note blamed target mix; that is wrong, the correlation with a team's share of steals of second is -0.0667, and the driver is the season. Both series are published with the decomposition attached. TEAM ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT where it can be checked: derived offline from war_daily plate appearances, 19,130 games, 2,122 of 2,122 home and away against real home_org/away_org, 30 clubs a season at 161 to 163 games. CAPTURED SHARE IS NEGATIVE UNDER ALL THREE FROZEN POLICIES (-0.6626, -0.0556, -0.5452), computed against a BUDGET-MATCHED optimum: the unlimited optimum attempts on eight times the real volume and is published beside it rather than used as the denominator. Read it as a bound on available value, not a verdict on managers, because the heuristic sees p* exactly and is credited with the league rate in any spot it picks. WHAT IT DECIDES: a team-season is an UPPER BOUND on a manager, so fetching the manager entity to attribute this signal is not worth building FOR THIS FAMILY. It says nothing about the bullpen or the pinch hit. RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-10 after audit finding F07-02: the win model was fitted and queried on a POST-play score against a PRE-play base-out state, so every decision on this surface was priced on leaked values. Refit on the honest state; the gate battery was re-run rather than assumed and its verdict is unchanged (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, split-half 0.1098 inside its null band). The league running-game net flipped sign (+1.79 to -0.75 wins) and the served Brier claim reversed (the MLB feed now leads 0.157516 to 0.157678). RE-RUN 2026-09-11 after audit F02-01: the census repair moved the priced pool to 13,973 attempts, and the battery was re-run rather than assumed. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: season-controlled split-half 0.1085 inside [-0.1501, 0.1272].

models.notes: 2026-09-06 (A-CLAIM-4). THE DEFECT: _is_vintage_matched requires a debut year, so a prospect who never reached the majors CANNOT enter the flagship frame. Every published accuracy cell is measured on players who all made it, and the ones a grade got most wrong are exactly the ones who vanished. RESULT, a clean null as pre-registered: eFV vs FanGraphs +0.01564 against a floor of 0.0268, vs MLB Pipeline +0.00231 against 0.0229. Nominally ahead of both, inside the floor on both, and inside on all four per-side cells. TWO SCREENS FIRE: one player carrying 11.73 career WAR is not a bust, and eight MLBAM collisions are the same human reached by two routes. THE POOL MUST BE COMBINED, and the first build got that wrong: scored alone every bust has the same outcome, so the rank correlation is undefined and the bootstrap returns nothing. BLAST RADIUS VERIFIED by running the backtest with the lane stashed: every published cell was byte-identical with and without it. COHORT DRIFT: data/timeseries.json is gitignored so conftest cannot revert it, and a suite chunk regenerating it moved the vintage frame from 796 rows to 812 mid-session. This lane's null has room to spare either way; A-CLAIM-10's verdict did not, and flipped. ASYMMETRY CONTROL added the same day, because the registration asked for it and the first build skipped it: the bust half splits 374 preseason-final and 413 in-season-final, against the registration's predicted 375 and 419. All four control cells sit inside their own wider floors (FanGraphs +0.02613 against 0.0306 and +0.01899 against 0.0281; Pipeline -0.00095 against 0.0255 and +0.00416 against 0.0240), and the Pipeline sign flips between the subgroups, which is what a null looks like. models.notes: 2026-09-06 (A-CLAIM-13). THE MEASUREMENT: all three published raters carry resolvable block scale and eFV carries none. Net of each rater's own placebo, FanGraphs -0.02156, MLB Pipeline -0.02749, PROSPX consensus -0.02410, eFV -0.00214; the three raters clear their E_cond floors AND fall outside their permutation bands, eFV clears neither and sits inside its band. THE REGISTERED EXPECTATION IS REFUTED ON SIZE: the plan predicted MLB Pipeline at -0.0113, which is 0.93 of its floor and not resolvable; measured it is about three times that and resolves. The 'no verdict change' half HELD. IT IS THE BASE YEAR, NOT THE SIDE: every side-only cell sits inside its floor for all four raters, every rater year-only cell clears. The side scale, the half anybody would have guessed was doing the work, buys nothing measurable. The exposure explanation (older cohorts have had longer to accumulate WAR, and eFV already prices exposure) is a HYPOTHESIS and is not tested here. THE SIGN FLIPS: eFV minus consensus is -0.0071 on the pooled cell and +0.0145 on this view, and NEITHER resolves, on a view whose floor is the tighter of the two (0.0217 against 0.0303). That is the strongest available argument for publishing 'indistinguishable' rather than a direction. ONE CELL CLEARS AND IT IS A RECEIPT: eFV vs FanGraphs +0.05975 against 0.0345 with CI [0.0182, 0.1021]. Under the alpha-spending clause every read other than the one declared confirmatory read is descriptive, so this is not a claim, does not reach a page, and does not enter a Holm family. A ONE-DRAW PLACEBO IS NOT A PLACEBO: the first build permuted once and that draw said the transform explained all of eFV's loss and none of the raters'. At 200 draws the placebo mean is similar for every column (-0.006 to -0.011) and the reading reverses. 2026-10-03 (POSTEPOCH_3_RATER_SCALE_VIEW_REREAD). On the fWAR label (data/source_backtest.json rebuilt at epoch step Q, generated_at 2026-10-03T22:45:08Z) the three 2026-09-06 findings do not hold: the pooled vintage-matched delta (-0.0062) and the block view's eFV vs consensus point_delta (-0.00002) share a sign; FanGraphs, MLB Pipeline and the PROSPX consensus sit inside their placebo bands; and no rater's year-only delta clears its floor (FanGraphs -0.01232 against 0.0174, MLB Pipeline -0.01307 against 0.0167, consensus -0.01265 against 0.0181). At the step A snapshot (eWAR v2 label, generated_at 2026-10-02T15:51:28Z) the sign flip and the placebo findings held, and the base-year finding held for MLB Pipeline and the consensus only (FanGraphs -0.01808 at or under 0.0182). This describes the label, not the accuracy of either basis (epoch gate clause (l)), and nothing served changes. Recorded in docs/efv-2026-09-06/RATER_SCALE_VIEW.md under '2026-10-03: the view on the fWAR label'; the 2026-09-06 text above is kept as the record of that day.

models.notes: 2026-09-06 (A-CLAIM-3). THE PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION HELD: C1 and C2 stay unresolved on both cuts. On the clean receipt (n=356, base years 2017 to 2020, every weight 1.0) eFV against the consensus is -0.00010 against a floor of 0.0377, which is as close to a dead heat as this instrument can report; against MLB Pipeline +0.00129 against 0.0419. On the censored full cut (n=812, mean weight 0.805) consensus -0.00264 against 0.0215 and Pipeline +0.00335 against 0.0274. FanGraphs clears at 1.10x on the resolved cut (+0.05627 against 0.0513) and sits at exactly 1.00x on the censored one (+0.03362 against 0.0337): two adjacent cuts on either side of the threshold, which is a margin nobody quotes, and a receipt rather than a claim under the alpha-spending clause. ONE PLAN FIGURE CORRECTED: the registration says the clean cut is debuts through 2021; RESOLVED_THROUGH is 2025 and the window is six seasons, so it is 2020, and the artifact derives the boundary from the shipped constants. IT REFUTES A-CLAIM-13'S EXPOSURE EXPLANATION. On the same 356 rows with only the label changed, not one rater's base-year block effect shrank and all four grew slightly (FanGraphs -0.0338 to -0.0370, Pipeline -0.0300 to -0.0319, consensus -0.0452 to -0.0468, eFV -0.0222 to -0.0337), while the label DID compress the between-block outcome spread from sd 2.611 to sd 1.575 and the range from 7.45 to 4.86 WAR. About forty percent of the between-block dispersion in the outcome was removed and the effect did not move. At 356 rows the block effect is not itself resolvable, so what is refuted is the mechanism's predicted DIRECTION, not the existence of some exposure component too small to see. The next candidate is grade drift and the per-block mean grade is now published so it can be looked at; it is not measured.

models.notes: 2026-09-06. A LIVE DEFECT IN A SHIPPED LABEL: 130 of 354 inductees never entered the ledger, 63 of them inside the eligible universe, and label_any called Charlie Gehringer, Ed Delahanty, Eddie Plank, Buck Ewing and Jesse Burkett non-Hall-of-Famers. 33 carried a resolved ZERO and 30 read as censored. The bridge was on disk the whole time. Ledger 226 to 306, label_any positives 223 to 286, zero lost, label_bbwaa byte-identical. THIS BUYS NO ACCURACY AND IS NOT EXPECTED TO. Its likely effect on a downstream bake-off is NEGATIVE: the recovered positives are heavily the 1930s and 1940s veterans wave and carry lower JAWS than the existing positive class. It also makes the plaque-role problem LARGER, because the players it recovers include managers who also played (Connie Mack, Casey Stengel, Bucky Harris, Al Lopez, Billy Southworth). 147 inductees inside the eligible universe now carry an unverified plaque role, so no Hall-sized line, no snub list and no deserved-versus-inducted verdict may be published until H-DATA-PLAQUE lands. The 48 the crosswalk cannot reach are overwhelmingly people who never played: umpires, owners, commissioners, union leaders and Negro Leagues pioneers. THREE BUGS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT. _BALLOT_CACHE was keyed on the path alone while the crosswalk changes the result, so inside one process the first call won and the label layer was call-order dependent; clear_cache cleared two of four caches; and crosswalk_bbref_mlbam returned its own cache dict, so clear_cache emptied a live reference and the producer serialized zero pairs into the artifact documenting 23,681. A FOURTH WAS FOUND BY A TEST, not by reasoning: the ingest applies the five percent drop flag back to 1936 where no such rule existed, and restricting to 1979 is NOT enough, because 88 non-elected players carry a flag on a year they went on to survive. Harvey Haddix is flagged in 1979 and appears through 1985; Edd Roush is flagged five times from 1936 and appears through 1960. resolution_year now requires the flag to sit on the LAST appearance. The BBWAA panel has TEN empty years, not the five the ingest records, because the writers voted biennially from 1956 to 1966: resolving a departed candidate at last plus one would name a non-existent election for 224 players. label_any is NON-MONOTONE in as-of year for 44 players (Joe Gordon closed 1945, inducted 2009), so no general as-of identity is claimed. [2026-09-24 second repair: four Negro Leagues inductees the crosswalk could not reach (Josh Gibson, Oscar Charleston, Cool Papa Bell, Ray Brown) each carry a full war_daily row, and StatsAPI names them by MLBAM ids the parquets do not carry. hof_data.NEGRO_LEAGUES_ID_BRIDGE bridges them, keyed on the MLBAM id and matched on birth date against the Chadwick register, never on a name. Ledger 306 to 310, unresolved 48 to 44, label_any positives 286 to 290, plaque role unverified inside the eligible universe 147 to 151, label_bbwaa byte-identical (data/hof_ledger_eval.json).]

models.notes: 2026-09-06. THE BAR IS 0.9697 AND IT IS NOT OURS. On label_bbwaa (1,219 players, 139 elected, 11.4 percent base rate) Baseball-Reference's HoF Monitor reaches AUC 0.9697 and EVERY in-house column loses to it above its own floor and survives Holm: career WAR -0.02546 against 0.0142, JAWS -0.02818, positive WAA -0.02710, WAR7 -0.04443, WAR ink -0.07897. PREDICTION 1 HELD. IT IS A MISSING-DATA STATEMENT, NOT A MODELLING FAILURE. HoF Monitor counts batting titles, MVP shares, All-Star selections and postseason play, none of which is in our feature set. Our shelf reproduces the public WAR shelf almost exactly; WAR alone simply orders these outcomes less well than a rule that also counts awards. PREDICTION 3 HELD ON THE PRIMARY LABEL AND FAILED ON THE SENSITIVITY: 13 of 30 calibration cells clear Holm on label_bbwaa (under half, as registered) and 18 of 30 on label_any (over half). The calibration-ERROR leg resolves NOTHING on either label, which is the half of the prediction that was exactly right. THE GUARD THAT WOULD HAVE SENT A BUILDER HUNTING A PHANTOM: pooled post-Platt AUC does NOT equal pooled raw AUC, because a mixture of fold-specific monotone maps is not one monotone map. Measured shift -0.0015 to -0.0181. The PER-FOLD check, which is the real guard, holds at exactly 0.0 over 165 checks. label_any is a disclosed sensitivity and its pooled comparison is REFUSED: 17 rows drop for want of a shelf row and every one is a positive (Roberto Clemente, Monte Irvin, Buck Leonard, Judy Johnson and the rest of the Negro Leagues honourees and manager inductions). A 90 percent positive-share threshold would not have fired on 17 of 286, which is exactly the case it would have existed for, so the rule is route concentration instead. POPULATION: this is NOT the eligible universe. It is almost exactly the set of players a screening committee already advanced to a ballot page, and an AUC here is discrimination among those candidates. That sentence travels with every number. TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY THE TESTS: the refusal path itself crashed with a ValueError when the gate doc sat outside the repo, and dropping empty fold blocks made the published chain jump from 2027 to 2033, which reads as a broken forward chain. [2026-09-24: after the ledger's second repair the label_any shelf hole is 21 of 290 positives (was 17 of 286), still all positives; the scored label_any frame (918 rows) and every AUC, floor and calibration cell on both labels are unchanged. Addendum in docs/HOF_BAKEOFF_GATE.md under G-8.]

models.notes: 2026-09-06. THE LEAGUE STEALS SECOND AT ITS OWN BREAK-EVEN: 75.00 percent success against a swing-weighted break-even of 75.03 percent over 11,977 attempts, which is -0.19 wins for the entire league across eight seasons. Steals of third PAY (+4.31 wins on 1,932 attempts, 76.14 percent against a 72.84 percent break-even) and steals of home do not (-2.33 on 62). Net across 19,130 games: +1.79 wins, against an absolute redistributable pool of 30.96. 57.18 percent of steal-of-second attempts sit BELOW their own break-even while the aggregate is a coin, because the good spots carry more swing. WHICH BREAK-EVEN MATTERS: the swing-weighted one. A reader comparing the success rate against the MEDIAN break-even gets the sign wrong on second. 9,328 two-out attempts are EXCLUDED and counted [CORRECTED 2026-09-11, audit F02-01: that count missed the two-out caught stealings that ended a plate appearance, which were neither priced nor counted. The repaired count is 11,783 of 26,139 attempts, and the page now states the census beside the table]: a caught stealing with two down ends the inning, so the alternative comes from the measured half-inning-start table while the hold comes from the smooth model, and nothing calibrates those two estimators against each other. Across three builds that mismatch priced 8.7 to 19.2 percent of attempts so that being CAUGHT STEALING HELPED the batting team.

models.notes: 2026-09-06. NO PLUS METRIC, BY GATE RATHER THAN BY TASTE. The battery frozen in docs/IN_GAME_MANAGEMENT_GATE.md returned DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: the season-controlled split-half correlation of a club's decision value is 0.0691 inside a permutation band of [-0.1504, 0.1243] over 238 club-seasons. The RAW split-half is 0.7789 and looks like a strong repeatable skill; it is a season effect, because both halves of a club-season sit in the same season. Season explains 79.6 percent of the variance in a club-season's summed decision value and the club explains 2.2 percent. THE NULL IS BOUNDED, which is what makes it publishable: the battery would have detected a true per-club effect of 0.0005 wins per attempt at 80 percent power. That is a ceiling, not a shrug. The club board therefore carries VOLUME and STYLE only, and the payload states why rather than leaving the omission to be noticed. Manager attribution is dark and DECIDED rather than deferred: a team-season is an upper bound on a manager, and building the manager entity to attribute a signal that is not there would be work spent making a null more precise. It says nothing about the bullpen or the pinch hit, which have not been measured. RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-10 after audit finding F07-02: the win model was fitted and queried on a POST-play score against a PRE-play base-out state, so every decision on this surface was priced on leaked values. Refit on the honest state; the gate battery was re-run rather than assumed and its verdict is unchanged (DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, split-half 0.1098 inside its null band). The league running-game net flipped sign (+1.79 to -0.75 wins) and the served Brier claim reversed (the MLB feed now leads 0.157516 to 0.157678).

models.notes: PROVISIONAL, NOT VALIDATED, and the distinction is the point: it carries an artifact because the artifact is what it PUBLISHES, not a forward record. 2026-09-06. UNVALIDATED AND SAYS SO. No captured market, no backtest, no forward record. What shipped today is a correctness repair plus honest error bars, not evidence the numbers are right. TWO LIVE DEFECTS FIXED. Milwaukee served playoffPct 1.001, because the emit rounded divisionPct and wildcardPct separately and ADDED them, which is unbounded above; it now derives the part from the whole. And remaining_pairs skipped games in progress while the standings had not booked them either, so 10 live games of 291 vanished and TWENTY of thirty clubs were projected over a 161-game season (ARI ATL BAL BOS CHC CIN CLE DET HOU KCR LAA MIA MIL NYM PHI PIT SFG TBR TEX TOR). season_shortfall now makes that visible: nothing had ever checked that wins plus losses plus remaining equalled a season. THE BRACKET is the current format with no reseeding, byes for the top two seeds, and coin-flip tiebreaks that are DISCLOSED rather than modelled. Conservation holds on the served build: 2.001 pennants, 1.000 champions, 4.000 byes. INTERVALS ARE WILSON ON RAW COUNTS, never Wald on a rounded probability, because the Wald error is identically zero at 0 and n and 13 of 30 clubs sit at those rails. No probability is published with zero stated uncertainty. THE WIN-TOTAL BAND IS SCHEDULE NOISE ONLY, at a fixed talent point estimate: no parameter uncertainty, no drift, no injuries, no trades. It is narrower than a real forecast interval by an amount nothing has measured, and the key is named sfScheduleOnly so a reader cannot mistake it for a predictive probability. A BUG MY OWN TEST CAUGHT: the seeding tiebreak drew from the regular-season generator, so switching the bracket on moved playoffPct from 0.340 to 0.417 on the same seed. 2026-10-01: CHAMPION TEXT CORRECTED TO THE CODE. It said 'a blended true-talent estimate'; proj_export._attach_current_season feeds the simulator talent = prior_by_team, the pure roster prior, and the record and Pythagorean blend reach only curWins. The text now says what the code does; the simulator's input is unchanged, so no served odd moved.

UNDECIDED BOTH SIDES, and the verdict rule was fixed before the run: a player-clustered CI95 covering zero prints UNDECIDED. hit b2 +0.2203 CI95 [-0.0987, +0.5952]; pit b2 +0.1301 CI95 [-0.1509, +0.4191]. Both b2 are POSITIVE and neither interval excludes zero, so on debuted_km at this n the served model leg does not measurably improve on the consensus anchor. THE TWO NULLS DISAGREE ON THE HITTER SIDE: the permutation null gives p=0.048 while the bootstrap CI covers zero. The CI is what was pre-specified and is what the verdict follows; they differ because the permutation holds the sample fixed while the bootstrap also carries uncertainty about which players were drawn. The zero-information twin returns +0.0006 and -0.0015, so the estimator is sound. Regressors are WAR-scale only and NEVER the blend beside its own components (blend = (1-lam)*cons + lam*model is an exact linear combination). This does NOT license removing the model leg or moving lambda: an interval covering zero is a statement about power as much as effect.
